steps: Hang a long lemon spiral in a highball and fill with ice.
Add the brandy and bitters and top with ginger ale.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Ginger ale with bitters-free lemon spiral (the original Horse's Neck).

horse-s-neck.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

death-in-the-afternoon.title: Death in the Afternoon
death-in-the-afternoon.description: Absinthe topped with Champagne until it clouds, Hemingway's creation.

ingredients.item: cold vegan Champagne (such as Moët & Chandon Impérial)

steps: Pour the absinthe into a coupe or flute.
Slowly add Champagne until it turns milky.
death-in-the-afternoon.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

nasi-goreng.title: Nasi Goreng
nasi-goreng.description: Indonesian fried rice with sweet soy sauce and shrimp paste, topped with a fried egg.
steps: Fry the shallots, garlic, chile and shrimp paste in the oil until fragrant.
Add the chicken or shrimp and cook through.
Add the rice, kecap manis and soy sauce and toss over high heat until hot and lightly charred.
Serve topped with a fried egg, with cucumber, tomato and fried shallots.
nasi-goreng.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

queen-s-park-swizzle.title: Queen's Park Swizzle
queen-s-park-swizzle.description: Demerara rum swizzled with mint, lime and Angostura bitters in layers.
steps: Lightly press the mint in a Collins glass with the syrup and lime.
Add the rum, fill with crushed ice and swizzle until frosty.
Top with more ice and dash the bitters over the top.
queen-s-park-swizzle.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

ingredients.item: vegan sweet vermouth (such as Dolin Rouge)

steps: Rinse a chilled coupe with absinthe.
Stir the rest with ice and strain into the glass.
remember-the-maine.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

laksa.title: Curry Laksa
laksa.description: Malaysian noodle soup in a spicy coconut curry broth with shrimp, tofu puffs and sprouts.

ingredients.item: cilantro, mint, lime wedges and sliced chiles

steps: Fry the laksa paste in the oil for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the stock and coconut milk and simmer 10 minutes. Season with fish sauce and sugar.
Add the shrimp and tofu puffs and cook 2 to 3 minutes.
Divide the noodles and sprouts among bowls and ladle the broth over.
Top with herbs, chiles and lime.
laksa.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

ingredients.item: lettuce, mint, cilantro, Thai basil, pickled carrot and chiles

steps: Mix the pork with 1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp sugar, shallots, half the garlic and the pepper. Shape into small patties.
Grill or broil the patties until charred and cooked, about 4 minutes per side.
Stir the remaining fish sauce, sugar and garlic with the lime juice and warm water for the dipping broth.
Put the patties in bowls of the broth and serve with noodles, herbs and pickles to dip.
bun-cha.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Raspberry, lime and ginger beer.

ingredients.item: vegan ruby port (such as Cockburn's Special Reserve)

steps: Dry-shake everything, then shake again with ice.
Strain into a small chilled glass and grate nutmeg on top.
porto-flip.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

cochinita-pibil.title: Cochinita Pibil
cochinita-pibil.description: Yucatán slow-roasted pork marinated in achiote and citrus, with pickled red onions.

ingredients.item: pork shoulder, cut into large chunks
red onion, thinly sliced and soaked in lime juice with salt

steps: Blend the achiote, citrus juices, garlic, cumin, oregano and salt.
Coat the pork and marinate at least 4 hours or overnight.
Line a baking dish with banana leaves or foil, add the pork and marinade and wrap tightly.
Roast at 325°F for 3 1/2 to 4 hours until it shreds easily.
Shred and serve in tortillas with the pickled onions and salsa.
cochinita-pibil.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

huevos-rancheros.title: Huevos Rancheros
huevos-rancheros.description: Fried eggs on crisp corn tortillas with ranchero salsa, beans and fresh cheese.

ingredients.item: ranchero sauce or warm tomato salsa

steps: Fry the tortillas in oil until lightly crisp. Drain.
Fry the eggs to your liking.
Spread each tortilla with beans, top with an egg and spoon over the sauce.
Finish with queso fresco, avocado and cilantro.
huevos-rancheros.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

banh-mi.title: Pork Banh Mi
banh-mi.description: Vietnamese baguette with lemongrass pork, pickled vegetables, cilantro, chiles and mayo.

ingredients.item: Vietnamese baguettes or soft French rolls

steps: Toss the carrot and daikon in the sweetened vinegar and let stand 30 minutes.
Marinate the pork in the lemongrass, fish sauce, soy sauce and sugar for 20 minutes.
Sear the pork in a hot skillet until caramelized.
Split and toast the rolls, spread with mayonnaise and fill with pork, pickles, cucumber, cilantro and jalapeño.
banh-mi.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

mole-poblano.title: Mole Poblano
mole-poblano.description: Chicken in Puebla's rich, dark sauce of dried chiles, spices, nuts and chocolate.

ingredients.item: sesame seeds, plus more to serve

steps: Simmer the chicken in salted water until cooked, about 40 minutes. Keep the broth.
Toast the chiles briefly and soak in hot water 20 minutes.
Toast the almonds, sesame seeds, raisins, tortilla and bread in a little oil.
Blend everything except the chicken and chocolate with broth until very smooth.
Fry the sauce in oil for 10 minutes, add the chocolate and more broth and simmer 30 minutes until thick.
Add the chicken to warm through and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
mole-poblano.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

pupusas.title: Pupusas
pupusas.description: Salvadoran stuffed corn cakes with cheese and beans, served with curtido slaw.
steps: Mix the cabbage, carrot, vinegar, oregano and salt for the curtido and chill.
Mix the masa, water and a pinch of salt into a soft dough.
With wet hands, flatten a ball of dough, fill with cheese and beans, close and pat into a 1/2-inch disk.
Cook on a hot griddle 3 to 4 minutes per side until spotted brown.
Serve with curtido and salsa.
pupusas.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

pozole-rojo.title: Pozole Rojo
pozole-rojo.description: Mexican pork and hominy stew in a red chile broth, with crunchy toppings.

ingredients.item: shredded cabbage, radishes, onion, lime and tostadas

steps: Simmer the pork with the onion, half the garlic and salt in 3 quarts of water for 1 1/2 hours.
Soak the chiles in hot water, then blend with the remaining garlic, oregano and a cup of broth. Strain.
Add the chile puree and hominy to the pot and simmer 45 minutes.
Shred the pork and season.
Serve with the toppings.
pozole-rojo.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

peruvian-ceviche.title: Peruvian Ceviche
peruvian-ceviche.description: Fresh fish cured in lime juice with red onion, chile and cilantro, served with sweet potato and corn.

ingredients.item: very fresh firm white fish, cubed
corn, boiled and cut into rounds

steps: Toss the fish with the salt, garlic and chile.
Pour over the lime juice and let stand 10 to 15 minutes until the outside turns opaque.
Add the onion and cilantro.
Serve right away with sweet potato and corn.
peruvian-ceviche.note: Use the freshest, sushi-grade fish you can get.

tamales.title: Pork Tamales
tamales.description: Steamed masa dough wrapped in corn husks around red chile pork.
steps: Beat the lard until fluffy, then beat in the masa, baking powder, salt and broth until a bit of dough floats in water.
Mix the pork with the chile sauce.
Spread a thin layer of masa on each husk, add a spoon of filling and fold the sides and bottom over.
Stand the tamales upright in a steamer and steam 1 to 1 1/2 hours until the masa pulls away from the husk.
tamales.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

arepas.title: Arepas
arepas.description: Golden Venezuelan corn cakes split and stuffed with cheese and fillings.

ingredients.item: fillings: shredded beef, black beans or avocado

steps: Mix the masarepa, water and salt into a soft dough and rest 5 minutes.
Shape into 8 disks about 1/2 inch thick.
Cook in a lightly oiled skillet over medium heat 5 to 6 minutes per side until crusty.
Split open and stuff with cheese and fillings.
arepas.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

lomo-saltado.title: Lomo Saltado
lomo-saltado.description: Peruvian stir-fried beef with onions, tomatoes and soy, served with fries and rice.

ingredients.item: aji amarillo or yellow chile, sliced

steps: Season the beef and sear in a very hot wok in batches. Remove.
Stir-fry the onion and chile for 1 minute, then the garlic.
Return the beef, add the soy sauce and vinegar, then the tomatoes for 30 seconds.
Toss with cilantro and the fries and serve with rice.
lomo-saltado.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

beef-empanadas.title: Beef Empanadas
beef-empanadas.description: Flaky baked pastries filled with spiced beef, onion, olives and egg.
steps: Cook the onion and pepper until soft, add the beef and spices and cook through. Stir in the olives and cool.
Heat the oven to 400°F.
Fill each round with beef and a little egg, fold over and crimp the edges.
Brush with beaten egg and bake 20 to 25 minutes until golden.
beef-empanadas.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

choripan.title: Choripán
choripan.description: Argentine grilled chorizo sandwiches with bright chimichurri.
steps: Mix the parsley, garlic, oregano, pepper flakes, vinegar and oil with a pinch of salt for the chimichurri.
Grill the chorizo over medium heat 12 to 15 minutes, turning, until cooked through.
Split the sausages lengthwise and grill the cut side briefly.
Toast the rolls, add the chorizo and spoon on chimichurri.
choripan.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

takoyaki.title: Takoyaki
takoyaki.description: Japanese octopus-filled batter balls topped with sauce, mayo, bonito flakes and seaweed.

ingredients.item: takoyaki sauce, Japanese mayo, bonito flakes and aonori

steps: Whisk the flour, eggs, dashi and soy sauce into a thin batter.
Heat an oiled takoyaki pan and fill the holes with batter.
Drop in octopus, green onion, ginger and tempura bits.
After 1 to 2 minutes, turn each ball with a skewer, tucking in the edges, and keep turning until round and golden.
Top with sauce, mayo, bonito flakes and aonori.
takoyaki.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

cabbage-rolls.title: Stuffed Cabbage Rolls
cabbage-rolls.description: Cabbage leaves rolled around beef and rice, baked in a sweet-sour tomato sauce.
steps: Core the cabbage and boil it whole, peeling off 12 leaves as they soften. Trim the thick ribs.
Mix the meats, rice, onion, garlic, paprika, salt and pepper.
Roll a portion of filling in each leaf, tucking in the sides.
Mix the tomatoes, sugar and lemon juice. Spread some in a dish, add the rolls and cover with the rest.
Cover and bake at 350°F for 1 1/2 hours.
cabbage-rolls.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

goulash.title: Hungarian Goulash
goulash.description: Hearty Hungarian beef and paprika stew with peppers and potatoes.
steps: Brown the beef in the fat in batches. Remove.
Cook the onions slowly until golden, then off the heat stir in the paprika and caraway.
Add the garlic, tomato paste, beef and broth and simmer 1 1/2 hours.
Add the peppers and potatoes and simmer 30 minutes until tender. Season.
Serve with a dollop of sour cream if you like.
goulash.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

pork-schnitzel.title: Pork Schnitzel
pork-schnitzel.description: Thin pork cutlets in a crisp, golden breadcrumb coating, served with lemon.

ingredients.item: boneless pork chops, pounded to 1/4 inch
large eggs, beaten with 1 tbsp water
vegetable oil or lard, for frying

steps: Season the pork with salt and pepper.
Dredge in flour, dip in egg and coat lightly in breadcrumbs without pressing.
Shallow-fry in 1/2 inch of hot oil, swirling the pan, 2 to 3 minutes per side until puffed and golden.
Drain and serve with lemon wedges.
pork-schnitzel.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

sauerbraten.title: Sauerbraten
sauerbraten.description: German pot roast marinated for days in spiced vinegar, with a sweet-sour gingersnap gravy.
steps: Boil the vinegar, water, vegetables, spices and sugar with 1 tsp salt. Cool and pour over the beef.
Marinate in the fridge 3 days, turning daily.
Dry the beef and brown it in the oil, then add the strained marinade. Cover and simmer 2 1/2 to 3 hours.
Remove the beef. Stir the gingersnaps and raisins into the liquid and simmer until thick.
Slice the beef and serve with the gravy.
sauerbraten.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

japchae.title: Japchae
japchae.description: Korean sweet potato glass noodles stir-fried with beef and vegetables in sesame-soy sauce.
steps: Cook the noodles 6 minutes, rinse and cut a few times with scissors.
Mix the soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil and garlic. Marinate the beef in 2 tbsp of it.
Stir-fry the vegetables one at a time until just tender, then the beef.
Toss everything with the noodles and the rest of the sauce. Sprinkle with sesame seeds.
japchae.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

chicken-shawarma.title: Chicken Shawarma
chicken-shawarma.description: Spiced, charred chicken thighs wrapped in pita with garlic sauce, pickles and vegetables.
steps: Marinate the chicken in the yogurt, lemon, spices, garlic and salt for at least 2 hours.
Roast at 425°F or grill 20 minutes until charred and cooked. Rest and slice thinly.
Warm the pitas.
Fill with chicken, vegetables, pickles and sauce, and roll up.
chicken-shawarma.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

beef-kofta.title: Beef Kofta
beef-kofta.description: Grilled skewers of spiced ground beef and onion, served with yogurt sauce.

ingredients.item: small onion, grated and squeezed dry
plain yogurt with grated cucumber and mint

steps: Knead the meat with the onion, parsley, garlic, spices and salt until sticky.
Shape around skewers into long sausages.
Grill over medium-high heat 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until cooked.
Serve with the yogurt sauce, flatbread and salad.
beef-kofta.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

bratwurst-with-sauerkraut.title: Bratwurst with Sauerkraut
bratwurst-with-sauerkraut.description: Beer-simmered then seared bratwurst over warm sauerkraut with mustard.
steps: Simmer the brats and onion in the beer for 15 minutes.
Sear the brats in a hot skillet or grill until browned.
Warm the sauerkraut with the onions, butter and caraway.
Serve the brats on the sauerkraut with mustard.

okonomiyaki.title: Okonomiyaki
okonomiyaki.description: Japanese savory cabbage pancake with pork belly, topped with sauce, mayo and bonito flakes.

ingredients.item: okonomiyaki sauce, Japanese mayo, bonito flakes and aonori

steps: Whisk the flour, dashi and eggs, then fold in the cabbage and green onions.
Spread half the batter in an oiled pan into a thick round and lay pork belly on top.
Cook 5 minutes over medium heat, flip and cook 5 minutes more until the pork is crisp.
Top with sauce, mayo, bonito flakes and aonori. Repeat with the rest.
okonomiyaki.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

chicken-adobo.title: Chicken Adobo
chicken-adobo.description: Filipino chicken braised in vinegar, soy sauce, garlic and bay leaves until glossy.
steps: Combine the chicken, soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, bay leaves and peppercorns and marinate 30 minutes.
Brown the chicken in the oil skin side down, then add the marinade and 1/2 cup water.
Simmer, covered, 30 minutes, then uncovered 10 minutes until the sauce reduces. Stir in the sugar.
Serve with steamed rice.
chicken-adobo.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

mushroom-risotto.title: Mushroom Risotto
mushroom-risotto.description: Creamy Arborio rice with sautéed mushrooms, white wine and Parmesan.

ingredients.item: chicken or vegetable stock, kept hot

steps: Brown the mushrooms in the oil and 1 tbsp butter and set aside.
Cook the shallot in 1 tbsp butter, add the rice and toast 2 minutes.
Add the wine and stir until absorbed, then add the stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for 18 to 20 minutes until creamy and just tender.
Stir in the mushrooms, remaining butter and Parmesan. Season and top with parsley.
mushroom-risotto.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

pierogi.title: Potato and Cheese Pierogi
pierogi.description: Polish dumplings filled with potato and cheddar, pan-fried with butter and onions.
steps: Mix the flour, egg, sour cream, water and a pinch of salt into a soft dough. Rest 30 minutes.
Mix the potatoes and cheese and season.
Roll the dough thin and cut 3-inch circles. Fill, fold and pinch tightly.
Boil in salted water until they float, plus 2 minutes.
Fry the onion in the butter until golden, add the pierogi and fry until crisp. Serve with sour cream.
pierogi.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

stuffed-bell-peppers.title: Stuffed Bell Peppers
stuffed-bell-peppers.description: Bell peppers filled with beef, rice and tomato, baked under melted cheese.

ingredients.item: bell peppers, tops cut and seeded

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F.
Brown the beef with the onion and garlic, then stir in the rice, tomatoes, half the tomato sauce and seasoning.
Stand the peppers in a baking dish, fill them and top with the rest of the sauce.
Cover and bake 35 minutes, top with cheese and bake 10 minutes more.
stuffed-bell-peppers.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

chicken-cordon-bleu.title: Chicken Cordon Bleu
chicken-cordon-bleu.description: Chicken breasts rolled around ham and Swiss cheese, breaded and baked.
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F.
Lay a slice of ham and cheese on each breast, roll up and secure with toothpicks.
Dredge in flour, dip in egg and coat in panko mixed with the butter.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes until golden and 165°F inside.
Remove the toothpicks and serve with Dijon.
chicken-cordon-bleu.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

beef-bulgogi.title: Beef Bulgogi
beef-bulgogi.description: Thin slices of beef in a sweet soy, garlic and sesame marinade, quickly seared.
steps: Mix the soy sauce, sugar, pear, sesame oil, garlic and ginger. Marinate the beef 30 minutes or longer.
Cook in a very hot skillet in batches 2 to 3 minutes until caramelized.
Top with green onions and sesame seeds and serve with rice and lettuce leaves.
beef-bulgogi.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

steps: Shake the gin, brandy, lime and bitters with ice.

golden-cadillac.description: Galliano and white crème de cacao shaken with cream.
steps: Shake everything hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
golden-cadillac.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

lamb-tagine.title: Lamb Tagine
lamb-tagine.description: Moroccan lamb slow-cooked with warm spices, apricots and honey, finished with almonds.
steps: Brown the lamb in the oil. Remove.
Cook the onion, garlic and ginger, then the spices for 1 minute.
Return the lamb with the broth, cover and simmer 1 1/2 hours.
Add the apricots and honey and cook 30 minutes until the lamb is tender.
Top with almonds and serve with couscous.
lamb-tagine.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

thai-green-curry.title: Thai Green Curry
thai-green-curry.description: Chicken and vegetables in a fragrant green curry with coconut milk and Thai basil.
steps: Fry the curry paste in the oil and a few spoonfuls of thick coconut cream until fragrant.
Add the chicken and cook 3 minutes.
Add the rest of the coconut milk, eggplant and lime leaves and simmer 10 minutes.
Add the pepper and season with fish sauce and sugar.
Stir in the basil and serve with jasmine rice.
thai-green-curry.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

stinger.title: Stinger
stinger.description: Cognac and white crème de menthe, an after-dinner classic.
steps: Stir or shake with ice.
Strain into a coupe or over crushed ice.
stinger.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

chicken-piccata.title: Chicken Piccata
chicken-piccata.description: Thin chicken cutlets in a lemony butter and caper sauce.

ingredients.item: large chicken breasts, halved and pounded thin

steps: Season the chicken and dredge in flour.
Brown in the oil and 1 tbsp butter 3 minutes per side. Remove.
Add the broth, wine, lemon and capers and simmer until reduced by half.
Swirl in the remaining butter, return the chicken and top with parsley.
chicken-piccata.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

navy-grog.title: Navy Grog
navy-grog.description: Three rums with lime, grapefruit and honey over a cone of ice.
steps: Shake everything except the soda with ice.
Strain over crushed ice in a double rocks glass and top with soda.
navy-grog.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

toronto.title: Toronto
toronto.description: Rye with Fernet-Branca, sugar and bitters.
steps: Stir everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
toronto.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

bibimbap.title: Bibimbap
bibimbap.description: Korean rice bowl with seasoned vegetables, beef, a fried egg and gochujang sauce.
steps: Cook the beef with 1 tbsp soy sauce, sugar and 1 tsp sesame oil.
Season the spinach and sprouts with a little sesame oil, soy and salt. Sauté the carrot and zucchini separately.
Fry the eggs sunny side up.
Mix the gochujang with 1 tbsp sesame oil and a splash of water.
Fill bowls with rice, arrange the vegetables and beef on top, add an egg and serve with the sauce and sesame seeds.
bibimbap.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

beef-bourguignon.title: Beef Bourguignon
beef-bourguignon.description: French beef braised in red wine with bacon, mushrooms and pearl onions.
steps: Heat the oven to 325°F. Cook the bacon in a Dutch oven and remove. Brown the beef in the fat in batches.
Return the beef and bacon, toss with the flour, then add the wine, broth, tomato paste, garlic and herbs.
Cover and braise 2 1/2 hours. Add the carrots for the last hour.
Brown the onions and mushrooms in the butter and stir into the stew.
Season and serve with potatoes or crusty bread.
beef-bourguignon.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

southside.title: Southside
southside.description: Gin, lime, sugar and fresh mint, shaken.
steps: Shake everything with ice.
Double-strain into a chilled coupe.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake lime, syrup and mint and top with soda.

southside.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

jasmine.title: Jasmine
jasmine.description: Gin, Campari, orange liqueur and lemon. Tastes like grapefruit juice.
steps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
jasmine.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

osso-buco.title: Osso Buco
osso-buco.description: Milanese braised veal shanks in white wine and tomato, topped with gremolata.
steps: Tie each shank around the middle, season and dredge in flour. Brown well in the oil.
Cook the onion, carrot and celery until soft, add the wine and reduce by half.
Add the tomatoes and stock, return the shanks, cover and simmer 2 to 2 1/2 hours until very tender.
Mix the lemon zest, parsley and garlic for the gremolata.
Serve with saffron risotto or polenta, topped with gremolata.
osso-buco.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

naked-and-famous.title: Naked and Famous
naked-and-famous.description: Equal parts mezcal, yellow Chartreuse, Aperol and lime.
steps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
naked-and-famous.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

coq-au-vin.title: Coq au Vin
coq-au-vin.description: French chicken braised in red wine with mushrooms, bacon and onions.
steps: Cook the bacon and remove. Brown the seasoned chicken in the fat and remove.
Stir the flour into the fat, then add the wine, broth, tomato paste, garlic and herbs.
Return the chicken and bacon, cover and simmer 45 minutes.
Brown the mushrooms and onions in the butter, add to the pot and simmer 20 minutes more.
Season and serve with mashed potatoes or bread.
coq-au-vin.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

chicken-cacciatore.title: Chicken Cacciatore
chicken-cacciatore.description: Italian hunter-style chicken braised with tomatoes, peppers, mushrooms and herbs.
steps: Season and brown the chicken in the oil. Remove.
Cook the onion, pepper and mushrooms until soft, then add the garlic.
Add the wine and reduce, then the tomatoes and herbs.
Return the chicken, cover and simmer 35 to 40 minutes. Season and top with basil.
chicken-cacciatore.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

moussaka.title: Moussaka
moussaka.description: Greek baked layers of eggplant, spiced lamb sauce and creamy béchamel.
steps: Brush the eggplant with oil and roast at 425°F for 20 minutes until golden.
Brown the meat with the onion and garlic, add the tomatoes and spices and simmer 20 minutes.
Melt the butter, whisk in the flour, then the milk and cook until thick. Off the heat, whisk in the yolks and half the cheese.
Layer half the eggplant, the meat, then the rest of the eggplant in a dish. Pour over the béchamel and top with cheese.
Bake at 350°F for 45 minutes until golden. Rest 20 minutes before cutting.
moussaka.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

beef-wellington.title: Beef Wellington
beef-wellington.description: Beef tenderloin wrapped in mushroom duxelles, prosciutto and golden puff pastry.
steps: Season and sear the beef on all sides in the oil. Brush with mustard and cool.
Cook the mushrooms and shallots in the butter until all the moisture is gone. Cool.
Lay the prosciutto overlapping on plastic wrap, spread with the mushrooms, set the beef on top and roll tightly. Chill 20 minutes.
Wrap in the rolled-out pastry, seal, brush with egg and chill 15 minutes.
Bake at 425°F for 35 to 40 minutes until 125°F inside for medium-rare. Rest 10 minutes before slicing.
beef-wellington.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

airmail.title: Airmail
airmail.description: Rum, lime and honey topped with Champagne.

ingredients.item: vegan Champagne (such as Moët & Chandon Impérial)

steps: Shake the rum, lime and honey with ice.
Strain into a flute and top with Champagne.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Lime and honey topped with alcohol-free sparkling wine.

airmail.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

army-and-navy.title: Army and Navy
steps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
army-and-navy.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

nigerian-suya.title: Nigerian Suya
nigerian-suya.description: Spicy grilled beef skewers coated in a peanut and chile spice blend.

ingredients.item: gluten-free bouillon cube (such as Herb-Ox), crushed
sliced red onion, tomatoes and cabbage

steps: Mix the ground peanuts, spices and bouillon to make yaji spice.
Toss the beef with the oil and most of the spice and marinate 1 hour.
Thread onto skewers and grill 5 to 6 minutes per side.
Dust with more spice and serve with onion, tomato and cabbage.
nigerian-suya.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

west-african-egusi-soup.title: Egusi Soup
west-african-egusi-soup.description: West African stew thickened with ground melon seeds, with greens and meat or fish.

ingredients.item: scotch bonnet peppers, blended with 2 tomatoes
beef or goat, cooked, with its stock

steps: Mix the egusi with a little water into a paste.
Heat the palm oil, cook the onion, then add the pepper and tomato blend and cook 10 minutes.
Add the egusi in spoonfuls and fry gently 10 minutes, stirring.
Add the meat with 3 cups stock, the fish, crayfish and bouillon and simmer 20 minutes.
Stir in the greens, cook 5 minutes and season. Serve with fufu or pounded yam.
west-african-egusi-soup.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

ethiopian-tibs.title: Ethiopian Tibs
ethiopian-tibs.description: Sautéed beef cubes with onion, peppers, rosemary and spiced butter.
steps: Sear the beef in a very hot skillet with half the butter until browned. Remove.
Cook the onion, jalapeños, garlic and ginger in the remaining butter.
Return the beef with the berbere and rosemary and toss 2 to 3 minutes.
Season and serve with injera.
ethiopian-tibs.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

jollof-rice.title: Jollof Rice
jollof-rice.description: West African rice cooked in a smoky, spiced tomato and pepper sauce.
steps: Blend the tomatoes, peppers, scotch bonnet and 1 onion until smooth.
Cook the other onion, sliced, in the oil, then fry the tomato paste 3 minutes.
Add the blended sauce, spices and bay leaves and cook 15 minutes until reduced.
Stir in the rice and stock, season, cover tightly and cook on low 30 minutes until tender.
Let the bottom toast slightly for a smoky flavor, then fluff and serve.
jollof-rice.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

ghanaian-red-red.title: Ghanaian Red Red
ghanaian-red-red.description: Black-eyed peas stewed in red palm oil and tomato, served with fried plantains.
steps: Heat the palm oil and cook the onion, garlic, ginger and pepper until soft.
Add the tomatoes and simmer 15 minutes.
Add the black-eyed peas and 1/2 cup water and simmer 15 minutes, mashing a few. Season.
Fry the plantains until caramelized and serve alongside.
ghanaian-red-red.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

senegalese-thieboudienne.title: Thieboudienne
senegalese-thieboudienne.description: Senegal's national dish of fish and vegetables cooked in tomato, with the rice cooked in the broth.

ingredients.item: cassava or sweet potato, in chunks

steps: Cut slits in the fish and stuff with the rof. Brown the fish in the oil and remove.
Cook the onion, then the tomato paste for 5 minutes. Add 8 cups water and the bouillon.
Add the vegetables and fish and simmer until each is tender, lifting them out as they are done.
Measure about 4 1/2 cups of the broth into the pot, add the rice, cover and cook on low 25 minutes.
Serve the rice topped with the fish and vegetables.
senegalese-thieboudienne.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

south-african-bobotie.title: South African Bobotie
south-african-bobotie.description: Curried, gently sweet minced beef baked under a savory egg custard.

ingredients.item: white bread, soaked in 1 cup milk

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F.
Cook the onion and garlic, add the beef and brown, then the spices for 1 minute.
Squeeze the bread, keeping the milk, and mix it into the beef with the jam, raisins, almonds and lemon juice.
Spread in a baking dish. Whisk the eggs with the saved milk, pour over and top with bay leaves.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes until the custard is set and golden.
south-african-bobotie.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

persian-tahdig.title: Persian Tahdig
persian-tahdig.description: Saffron basmati rice with a crunchy golden crust from the bottom of the pot.

ingredients.item: saffron, ground and steeped in 3 tbsp hot water

steps: Boil the rice in plenty of salted water for 6 minutes and drain.
Mix 1 1/2 cups of the rice with the yogurt and half the saffron.
Heat the oil and half the butter in a nonstick pot and press the yogurt rice firmly over the bottom.
Mound the rest of the rice on top, poke holes, drizzle with butter and saffron. Wrap the lid in a towel and cover.
Cook 10 minutes on medium, then 50 minutes on low. Turn out onto a plate so the crust is on top.
persian-tahdig.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

moroccan-harira.title: Moroccan Harira
moroccan-harira.description: Spiced tomato, lentil and chickpea soup, traditional for breaking the Ramadan fast.
steps: Brown the meat in the oil with the onion and celery, then add the spices.
Add the tomatoes, water and lentils and simmer 40 minutes.
Add the chickpeas and vermicelli and simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in the flour mixture to thicken and the herbs. Season and serve with lemon.
moroccan-harira.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

egyptian-koshari.title: Egyptian Koshari
egyptian-koshari.description: Rice, lentils and pasta topped with spicy tomato sauce, chickpeas and crispy onions.
steps: Fry the onions in the oil until dark and crisp. Drain, keeping the oil.
Cook the lentils 15 minutes, add the rice, a spoon of onion oil and water to cover, and cook until both are tender.
Boil the macaroni.
Cook the garlic in a little oil, add the tomato sauce, cumin, chili and vinegar and simmer 10 minutes.
Layer rice and lentils, macaroni, chickpeas and sauce, and top with crispy onions.
egyptian-koshari.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

indian-pav-bhaji.title: Pav Bhaji
indian-pav-bhaji.description: Mumbai street food: buttery mashed spiced vegetables with toasted soft rolls.

ingredients.item: butter, plus more for the rolls
lemon wedges, chopped onion and cilantro

steps: Mash the potatoes, cauliflower and peas.
Cook the onion and pepper in butter, add the ginger-garlic paste, tomatoes and masala and cook until soft.
Add the mashed vegetables and 1 cup water and mash everything together. Simmer 10 minutes.
Split the rolls and toast in butter.
Serve the bhaji topped with butter, onion and cilantro, with lemon and the rolls.
indian-pav-bhaji.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

pakistani-nihari.title: Pakistani Nihari
pakistani-nihari.description: Slow-cooked beef shank stew with deep spices, thickened with flour and topped with ginger and chiles.

ingredients.item: atta or all-purpose flour mixed with 1 cup water
julienned ginger, green chiles, cilantro and lemon

steps: Cook the onion in the ghee until golden, then the ginger-garlic paste and spices.
Add the beef and brown, then cover with 10 cups water and simmer very gently 4 hours until it falls apart.
Stir in the flour slurry and simmer 20 minutes until thick and glossy. Season.
Serve with the ginger, chiles, cilantro and lemon, and naan.
pakistani-nihari.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

tunisian-couscous.title: Tunisian Couscous
tunisian-couscous.description: Couscous with lamb and vegetables in a spicy harissa and tomato broth.
steps: Brown the lamb and onion in the oil, then add the tomato paste, harissa and spices.
Add 6 cups water and simmer 45 minutes.
Add the carrots and potato, then the zucchini and chickpeas, and cook until tender.
Steam or soak the couscous in some of the broth with a little oil.
Mound the couscous, top with meat and vegetables and ladle over broth.
tunisian-couscous.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

lebanese-kibbeh.title: Lebanese Kibbeh
lebanese-kibbeh.description: Fried bulgur and lamb shells stuffed with spiced meat, onions and pine nuts.

ingredients.item: fine bulgur, soaked 15 minutes and squeezed
very lean ground lamb or beef, for the shell

steps: Process the bulgur, lean meat, grated onion, half the spices and salt into a smooth paste, using ice water if needed.
For the filling, brown the ground lamb with the chopped onion, pine nuts and remaining spices.
Shape a ball of shell mix, hollow it with your finger, fill and seal into an oval.
Fry at 350°F for 5 to 6 minutes until deep brown. Serve with yogurt.
lebanese-kibbeh.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

indian-baingan-bharta.title: Baingan Bharta
indian-baingan-bharta.description: Smoky fire-roasted eggplant mashed with onion, tomato and spices.
steps: Roast the eggplants over a flame or under the broiler, turning, until charred and collapsed. Peel and mash.
Fry the cumin seeds in oil, add the onion until golden, then the ginger-garlic and chile.
Add the tomatoes and spices and cook until soft.
Stir in the eggplant and cook 5 minutes. Season and top with cilantro.
indian-baingan-bharta.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

indian-aloo-gobi.title: Aloo Gobi
indian-aloo-gobi.description: Potatoes and cauliflower cooked with turmeric, cumin and ginger.
steps: Fry the cumin seeds in oil, add the onion and cook until soft, then the ginger and chile.
Add the tomato and spices for 2 minutes.
Add the potatoes and cauliflower with salt, cover and cook on low 15 to 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until tender.
Sprinkle with garam masala and cilantro.
indian-aloo-gobi.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

turkish-lahmacun.title: Turkish Lahmacun
turkish-lahmacun.description: Thin, crisp flatbreads topped with spiced minced lamb, rolled up with herbs and lemon.

ingredients.item: lemon wedges, parsley and sliced onion, to serve

steps: Heat the oven with a baking stone to 500°F.
Pulse the onion, pepper, tomatoes, garlic and parsley finely, then mix with the lamb, pepper paste, spices and salt.
Roll the dough into very thin rounds and spread thinly with the topping.
Bake 6 to 8 minutes until crisp at the edges.
Squeeze with lemon, scatter parsley and onion, and roll up to eat.
turkish-lahmacun.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

indian-rajma-chawal.title: Rajma Chawal
indian-rajma-chawal.description: Punjabi kidney bean curry in a thick onion-tomato gravy, served with rice.

ingredients.item: each coriander, cumin and chile powder

steps: Fry the cumin seeds, then cook the onion until browned and add the ginger-garlic paste.
Add the tomatoes and spices and cook until the oil separates.
Add the beans and 2 cups water and simmer 25 minutes, mashing a few beans.
Stir in the garam masala and cilantro and serve over rice.
indian-rajma-chawal.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

georgian-khachapuri.title: Adjarian Khachapuri
georgian-khachapuri.description: Boat-shaped Georgian bread filled with molten cheese, topped with an egg and butter.
steps: Heat the oven to 475°F.
Divide the dough into 4 ovals. Roll the long sides in toward the middle and twist the ends to make boats.
Fill the centers with the mixed cheeses.
Bake 12 to 15 minutes until golden.
Drop an egg yolk and a pat of butter into each and bake 1 to 2 minutes more. Stir together at the table and tear off the crust to dip.
georgian-khachapuri.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

filipino-kare-kare.title: Filipino Kare-Kare
filipino-kare-kare.description: Oxtail and vegetables in a rich peanut sauce, served with shrimp paste.

ingredients.item: annatto oil or 1 tsp annatto powder

steps: Simmer the oxtail in water for 2 1/2 to 3 hours until tender. Keep 4 cups of the broth.
Cook the onion and garlic, add the broth, peanut butter, ground rice and annatto and simmer until thick.
Add the oxtail, then the beans and eggplant, and cook until tender. Add the bok choy last.
Serve with rice and bagoong on the side.
filipino-kare-kare.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

indian-idli-sambar.title: Idli Sambar
indian-idli-sambar.description: Soft steamed rice cakes with tangy lentil and vegetable stew.

ingredients.item: idli batter (fermented rice and urad dal)

steps: Grease the idli molds, fill with batter and steam 10 to 12 minutes until set.
Cook the toor dal until soft and mash.
Cook the vegetables, onion and tomato in water until tender, then add the tamarind, sambar powder, dal and salt and simmer 10 minutes.
Fry the mustard seeds and curry leaves in oil and pour over the sambar.
Serve the idli with the sambar and coconut chutney.
indian-idli-sambar.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

georgian-khinkali.title: Georgian Khinkali
georgian-khinkali.description: Large twisted soup dumplings filled with spiced beef and pork in juice.

ingredients.item: salt and plenty of black pepper

steps: Knead the flour, warm water and salt into a firm dough. Rest 30 minutes.
Mix the meats, onion, herbs, spices and salt, then work in the cold water until loose.
Roll the dough and cut 4-inch circles. Add filling and gather the edge into many pleats, twisting the top into a knot.
Boil in salted water 10 to 12 minutes.
Dust with pepper. Bite a hole, sip the juice, and leave the knot.
georgian-khinkali.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

filipino-pancit.title: Filipino Pancit Bihon
filipino-pancit.description: Thin rice noodles stir-fried with chicken, shrimp and vegetables, served with calamansi.
steps: Cook the garlic and onion in the oil, then the chicken until cooked, then the shrimp.
Add the vegetables and cook 2 minutes.
Add the broth, soy sauce and oyster sauce and bring to a boil.
Add the noodles and toss until they absorb the liquid.
Serve with calamansi wedges.
filipino-pancit.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

korean-tteokbokki.title: Korean Tteokbokki
korean-tteokbokki.description: Chewy rice cakes simmered in a sweet and spicy gochujang sauce with fish cakes.
steps: Soak the rice cakes in warm water if they are hard.
Bring the broth to a boil and stir in the gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce and sugar.
Add the rice cakes and simmer 8 to 10 minutes, stirring, until soft and the sauce thickens.
Add the fish cakes, green onions and eggs and cook 3 minutes more.
korean-tteokbokki.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

sri-lankan-kottu-roti.title: Sri Lankan Kottu Roti
sri-lankan-kottu-roti.description: Chopped flatbread stir-fried on a griddle with vegetables, egg, chicken and curry sauce.

ingredients.item: paratha or roti, cut into thin strips
cooked chicken curry, shredded, with 1/2 cup sauce

steps: Fry the onion, curry leaves and chiles in the oil, then the leek, carrot and cabbage for 3 minutes.
Push aside and scramble the eggs.
Add the chicken and roti strips and chop and toss everything together with two spatulas.
Add the curry sauce, season and toss until hot.
sri-lankan-kottu-roti.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

filipino-sinigang.title: Filipino Sinigang
filipino-sinigang.description: Sour tamarind soup with pork and vegetables.

ingredients.item: pork spareribs or belly, in pieces

steps: Simmer the pork, onion and tomatoes in 10 cups water for 45 minutes, skimming.
Add the tamarind mix and daikon and simmer 5 minutes.
Add the beans, eggplant and chiles and cook until tender.
Add the greens and fish sauce and serve with rice.
filipino-sinigang.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

armenian-dolma.title: Armenian Dolma
armenian-dolma.description: Grape leaves rolled around beef, rice and herbs, simmered in a lemony broth.

ingredients.item: plain yogurt mixed with 1 grated garlic clove, to serve

steps: Mix the beef, rice, onion, herbs, tomato paste and spices.
Place a leaf vein side up, add a spoon of filling, fold in the sides and roll tightly.
Pack the rolls seam side down in a pot lined with spare leaves.
Add the broth and lemon juice, weigh down with a plate and simmer 1 hour.
Serve with garlic yogurt.
armenian-dolma.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

japanese-oyakodon.title: Japanese Oyakodon
japanese-oyakodon.description: Chicken and onion simmered in sweet dashi and soy, set with egg over rice.
steps: Simmer the dashi, soy sauce, mirin and sugar with the onion for 3 minutes.
Add the chicken and cook 5 minutes.
Pour the eggs over, cover and cook 1 minute until softly set.
Slide over bowls of rice and top with herbs.
japanese-oyakodon.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

korean-sundubu-jjigae.title: Korean Sundubu Jjigae
korean-sundubu-jjigae.description: Bubbling spicy soft tofu stew with seafood and an egg.
steps: Cook the pork in the oil, then add the gochugaru and garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the broth and soy sauce and bring to a boil.
Add the seafood and spoon in big pieces of tofu. Simmer 5 minutes.
Crack in the egg, add green onions and cook 1 minute. Serve bubbling with rice.
korean-sundubu-jjigae.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

indonesian-beef-rendang.title: Indonesian Beef Rendang
indonesian-beef-rendang.description: Dry, deeply spiced beef curry slow-cooked in coconut milk until caramelized.
steps: Blend the shallots, garlic, ginger, galangal, chiles, 1 lemongrass and turmeric into a paste.
Fry the paste in oil 5 minutes, add the beef and coat.
Add the coconut milk, remaining lemongrass and lime leaves and simmer uncovered 2 1/2 to 3 hours, stirring more often as it thickens.
Stir in the kerisik and sugar and cook until the sauce is dark and clings to the beef. Season with salt.
indonesian-beef-rendang.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

persian-fesenjan.title: Persian Fesenjan
persian-fesenjan.description: Chicken stewed in a rich, sweet-sour sauce of ground walnuts and pomegranate molasses.
steps: Toast the walnuts and grind very fine.
Brown the chicken and onion in the oil.
Add the walnuts and broth and simmer 30 minutes, stirring.
Add the pomegranate molasses, cinnamon, sugar and salt and simmer 45 minutes until thick and dark.
Top with pomegranate seeds and serve with rice.
persian-fesenjan.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

japanese-unagi-don.title: Japanese Unagi Don
japanese-unagi-don.description: Grilled eel glazed in sweet tare sauce over rice.
steps: Simmer the soy sauce, mirin, sugar and sake until syrupy to make the tare.
Brush the eel with tare and broil 3 to 4 minutes until bubbling.
Spoon a little tare over the rice, add the eel and drizzle with more.

water-lily-cocktail.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

benton-s-old-fashioned.title: Benton's Old Fashioned
benton-s-old-fashioned.description: A bacon fat-washed bourbon Old Fashioned sweetened with maple syrup.
steps: Stir everything with ice.
Strain over a large cube and express an orange peel over it.
benton-s-old-fashioned.note: To fat-wash, stir 1 oz warm bacon fat into a 750 ml bottle of bourbon, freeze, then strain out the solid fat.

the-chancellor-cocktail.title: The Chancellor
the-chancellor-cocktail.description: Scotch, ruby port and dry vermouth with bitters.

ingredients.item: vegan ruby port (such as Cockburn's Special Reserve)
vegan dry vermouth (such as Dolin Dry)

steps: Stir everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
the-chancellor-cocktail.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

sherry-flip.title: Sherry Flip
sherry-flip.description: Sherry shaken with a whole egg and sugar, topped with nutmeg.

ingredients.item: vegan oloroso sherry (such as Barbadillo Oloroso Seco)

steps: Dry-shake everything, then shake again with ice.
Strain into a small chilled glass and grate nutmeg on top.
sherry-flip.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

iskender-kebab.title: Iskender Kebab
iskender-kebab.description: Turkish thin-sliced lamb over pide bread with tomato sauce, yogurt and browned butter.

ingredients.item: lamb or beef, very thinly sliced (or doner meat)

steps: Sear the meat in the oil until browned.
Simmer the tomato sauce with the pepper paste and a pinch of salt.
Toast the bread cubes and lay them on plates. Spoon some tomato sauce over.
Top with the meat and the rest of the sauce, with yogurt on the side.
Brown the butter with the paprika and pour over at the table.
iskender-kebab.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

division-bell-cocktail.title: Division Bell
steps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
division-bell-cocktail.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

improved-whiskey-cocktail.title: Improved Whiskey Cocktail
improved-whiskey-cocktail.description: Rye with maraschino, absinthe and bitters, a 19th-century classic.
steps: Stir everything with ice.
Strain into a rocks glass over a large cube.
improved-whiskey-cocktail.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

doro-wat.title: Doro Wat
doro-wat.description: Ethiopian chicken stew slow-cooked in berbere and spiced butter, with hard-boiled eggs.

ingredients.item: large red onions, very finely chopped

steps: Rub the chicken with lemon juice and salt.
Cook the onions in a dry pot over low heat 20 minutes, stirring, until soft and reduced.
Add the niter kibbeh, berbere, garlic and ginger and cook 10 minutes.
Add the chicken and broth and simmer 40 minutes.
Add the eggs and simmer 10 minutes more. Serve with injera.
doro-wat.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

bijou.title: Bijou
bijou.description: Gin, sweet vermouth and green Chartreuse in equal parts.

ingredients.item: vegan sweet vermouth (such as Dolin Rouge)

steps: Stir everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
bijou.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

adas-polo.title: Adas Polo (Persian Lentil Rice)
adas-polo.description: Fluffy saffron basmati layered with brown lentils and warm cinnamon, crowned with sweet caramelized onions, dates and raisins, with a crisp golden rice crust (tahdig) underneath.

ingredients.item: saffron threads, ground with a pinch of sugar
salt, for the rice water, plus more to taste
plain yogurt or Shirazi salad, to serve

steps: Rinse the rice in cool water until it runs almost clear, then soak it in salted water for at least 30 minutes. Bloom the saffron in the hot water.
Simmer the lentils in plenty of water for 15 to 20 minutes, until just tender but still holding their shape. Drain and season with a pinch of salt.

Cook the onions in the oil over medium heat for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden and sweet. Stir in the cinnamon and turmeric for 30 seconds, then lift out half the onions for the top.
Add 2 tbsp butter, the raisins and dates to the onions left in the pan and warm for 2 minutes, just until the raisins plump. Set aside.

Bring a large pot of water and 2 tbsp salt to a rolling boil. Drain the rice, add it and boil 5 to 6 minutes, until the grains are soft outside but still have a firm bite in the center. Drain and gently fold in the lentils.
Melt 2 tbsp butter in a heavy nonstick pot with 2 tbsp water and 1 tbsp of the saffron water. Spread a thin layer of rice over the bottom and press it down: this becomes the tahdig.
Pile the rest of the rice in a loose mound. Poke 4 or 5 holes down to the bottom with a spoon handle, dot with the remaining butter and drizzle with the rest of the saffron water.

Wrap the lid in a clean kitchen towel, cover tightly and cook 10 minutes on medium until you hear sizzling, then 40 to 45 minutes on low. Spoon onto a platter, scatter the fruit and onions over, and serve the crust broken into pieces.
adas-polo.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Parboiling then steaming is the Persian method that keeps every grain separate and long. Stop boiling the moment the outside is soft and the center still resists.
The towel under the lid catches steam that would otherwise drip back and make the rice soggy.
Listen for the sizzle before turning the heat down: it means the bottom is starting to crisp into tahdig.
adas-polo.make_ahead: Cook the lentils and onions up to 2 days ahead. Leftover rice keeps 4 days; reheat with a splash of water, covered, so it steams.
variations: With meat: brown 1 lb ground beef or lamb with onion and turmeric and serve it alongside.
Add 1/4 cup barberries, quickly warmed in butter with a pinch of sugar, for a tart contrast.

ajiaco.title: Ajiaco (Colombian Chicken and Potato Soup)
ajiaco.description: Bogotá's comforting soup of chicken, corn and three kinds of potato, flavored with the herb guascas. The floury potatoes melt into a thick broth, served with cream, capers and avocado.

ingredients.item: russet potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
papas criollas or baby yellow potatoes
Mexican crema or heavy cream, to serve

steps: Put the chicken, water, green onions, garlic, cilantro, salt and pepper in a large pot. Bring to a boil, skim, then simmer gently, partly covered, for 30 minutes.
Lift out the chicken and set it aside to cool. Discard the green onions and cilantro.
Add the corn, russet potatoes and red potatoes to the broth. Simmer 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the russets start to fall apart and thicken the soup.
Add the papas criollas and guascas and simmer 15 to 20 minutes more, until the small potatoes are tender and the broth is creamy. Mash a few potato slices against the pot if it needs more body.
Meanwhile, shred the chicken, discarding the skin and bones. Return it to the pot to warm through and taste for salt.
Ladle into deep bowls with a piece of corn in each. Serve the cream, capers and avocado at the table so everyone adds their own.
ajiaco.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: The three potatoes each do a job: russets dissolve to thicken, red potatoes hold their shape, and the little yellow ones add buttery flavor.
Guascas gives ajiaco its signature taste. Look for it dried in Latin markets; dried oregano is a distant but workable stand-in.
Keep the chicken at a gentle simmer so it stays tender enough to shred.
ajiaco.make_ahead: Keeps 3 days in the fridge and thickens as it sits; thin it with water when reheating. Add the cream, capers and avocado only when serving.
variations: Serve with a side of white rice, the way many Bogotá families do.

amok-trey.title: Amok Trey (Cambodian Fish Amok)
amok-trey.description: Cambodia's national dish: tender white fish in a silky coconut curry custard scented with lemongrass, galangal and lime leaf, steamed in banana-leaf cups.

ingredients.item: firm white fish (catfish, tilapia or cod), cut into bite-size pieces
lemongrass, tender parts only, thinly sliced
galangal or ginger, peeled and sliced
makrut lime leaves, stems removed (2 for garnish)
dried red chilies, soaked in hot water
coconut milk, plus 1/4 cup thick coconut cream for topping
red chili, cut in thin strips, to garnish

steps: Make the kroeung paste: pound or blend the lemongrass, galangal, turmeric, 2 lime leaves, shallots, garlic, drained chilies and shrimp paste with a splash of water until smooth.
Whisk the paste with the coconut milk, egg, fish sauce and sugar. Fold in the fish and let it sit 10 minutes.
Soften the banana leaves over a flame or in hot water and fold them into four cups, pinning the corners with toothpicks. Line each cup (or ramekin) with shredded spinach.
Spoon the fish and curry into the cups. Steam over simmering water, covered, for 20 to 25 minutes, until the custard is set but still trembles slightly and the fish flakes.
Top each with a spoon of coconut cream, finely shredded lime leaf and chili strips. Serve hot with rice.
amok-trey.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: The egg is what turns the curry into amok's soft, mousse-like custard. Steam gently: a hard boil makes it grainy.
Fresh kroeung is the soul of the dish. Make a double batch and freeze half for next time.
Cut the fish into even pieces so every piece cooks in the same time.
amok-trey.make_ahead: The kroeung paste keeps 1 week in the fridge or 3 months frozen. Amok is best eaten freshly steamed.
variations: Chicken amok: use thinly sliced chicken thigh and steam 25 minutes.

cape-malay-bredie.title: Cape Malay Tomato Bredie
cape-malay-bredie.description: South Africa's slow-cooked lamb and tomato stew, gently spiced with cinnamon, cloves and cardamom, until the lamb falls from the bone and the tomatoes turn jammy.

ingredients.item: lamb neck or shoulder chops, cut into large pieces
chili flakes or 1 fresh green chili, chopped
ripe tomatoes, chopped, or 2 cans (14 oz) chopped tomatoes
steamed rice and chopped parsley, to serve

steps: Season the lamb with salt and dust it lightly with flour. Brown it in the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat, in batches, for about 3 minutes a side. Set aside.
Lower the heat and cook the onions for 10 minutes until soft and golden. Add the garlic, ginger, cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, bay leaves and chili and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.

Add the tomatoes, tomato paste and sugar and return the lamb with its juices. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook gently for 1 1/2 hours, stirring now and then. Add a splash of water only if it starts to catch.
Add the potatoes and cook, covered, for 25 to 30 minutes more, until the potatoes are tender and the lamb pulls easily from the bone.
Uncover for the last 10 minutes if the sauce is thin. It should be thick and glossy. Taste for salt and sugar, then serve over rice with parsley.
cape-malay-bredie.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: The lamb braises in the tomatoes' own juice, so add water sparingly. A thick, jammy sauce is the goal.
A spoon of sugar balances the acidity of the tomatoes. Taste and add more if your tomatoes are sharp.
Bony cuts like neck give the richest sauce; boneless shoulder works too and cooks a little faster.
cape-malay-bredie.make_ahead: Like most stews it tastes better the next day. Keeps 4 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen.
variations: Green bean bredie: replace the tomatoes with 1 1/2 lb green beans and a cup of stock.
Pressure cooker: after browning and adding the tomatoes, cook 35 minutes on high, then add the potatoes for 6 minutes.

chakhchoukha.title: Chakhchoukha
chakhchoukha.description: An Algerian feast dish from the Aurès: thin semolina flatbread torn into pieces and soaked in marqa, a spiced tomato stew of lamb, chickpeas and vegetables.

ingredients.item: lamb shoulder, cut into large chunks
chickpeas, drained, or 1 cup dried, soaked overnight
rougag or thin semolina flatbread (or thin pita), torn into small pieces

steps: Brown the lamb in the oil in a large pot. Add the onion and garlic and cook 5 minutes, then stir in the tomato paste, tomatoes, ras el hanout, paprika, cayenne, pepper and salt for 2 minutes.
Add the water (and dried chickpeas if using). Bring to a boil, then simmer, covered, for 45 minutes.
Add the carrots (and canned chickpeas) and simmer 15 minutes, then the zucchini for 10 minutes more, until the lamb is tender and the sauce is rich and slightly reduced.
Meanwhile, steam the torn bread over the stew or in a steamer basket for 10 minutes, tossing once, until soft and pliable. Toss with the butter.
Pile the bread in a wide dish and ladle over plenty of the hot sauce, letting it soak in. Top with the lamb, chickpeas and vegetables and serve extra sauce on the side.
chakhchoukha.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Steaming the bread first makes it soft enough to drink up the sauce without turning to mush.
The sauce should be plentiful and thin enough to soak in, more like a broth than a thick stew.
chakhchoukha.make_ahead: The marqa stew keeps 3 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen. Steam and soak the bread just before serving.
variations: Use chicken pieces instead of lamb and simmer 35 minutes.

encebollado.title: Encebollado (Ecuadorian Tuna and Yuca Soup)
encebollado.description: Ecuador's beloved coastal soup: fresh tuna and tender yuca in a cumin-scented tomato broth, piled high with lime-pickled red onions. A famous hangover cure.

ingredients.item: fresh albacore or yellowfin tuna, in large pieces
yuca (cassava), fresh or frozen, peeled and cut in chunks
limes, juiced, plus wedges to serve
plantain chips (chifles), popcorn and hot sauce, to serve

steps: Make the curtido: soak the red onions in salted warm water for 5 minutes, drain, then toss with the diced tomatoes, lime juice, a pinch of salt and some cilantro. Let it sit while you cook.
Make a refrito: cook the white onion in the oil for 5 minutes, then add the chopped tomatoes, garlic, cumin and chili powder and cook 5 minutes more, until thick.
Add the water, salt and cilantro stems and bring to a boil. Add the tuna and simmer gently for 10 to 12 minutes, until just cooked. Lift it out and flake it into large chunks.
Add the yuca to the broth and simmer 25 to 30 minutes, until very tender. Remove the woody center strand from each piece, and mash a few pieces against the pot to thicken the broth.
Return the tuna, warm through and taste for salt. Serve in deep bowls, heaped with curtido, with chifles, lime wedges and hot sauce on the side.
encebollado.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Poaching the tuna first and returning it at the end keeps it moist instead of dry and stringy.
Frozen yuca is already peeled and cooks more evenly than fresh, and it works perfectly here.
The curtido is half the dish: the sharp, crunchy onions cut the rich broth.
encebollado.make_ahead: The broth and yuca keep 3 days in the fridge; add the tuna when reheating if you can. The curtido keeps 3 days.
variations: Use swordfish or mahi-mahi if fresh tuna is hard to find.

haitian-griot.title: Haitian Griot
haitian-griot.description: Haiti's celebration pork: shoulder marinated in citrus and epis, braised until tender, then fried until crisp and caramelized. Served with fiery pikliz and fried plantains.

ingredients.item: sour orange juice, or half orange and half lime juice
epis (blend of parsley, green onion, peppers, garlic, thyme and oil)
pikliz, fried plantains and rice, to serve

steps: Rinse the pork with the lime juice and water, then toss it with the sour orange juice, epis, onion, garlic, thyme, cloves, salt and pepper. Marinate at least 2 hours, or overnight in the fridge.
Put the pork and marinade in a heavy pot with the whole Scotch bonnet and enough water to come halfway up. Simmer, covered, for 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes, until tender.
Uncover and boil off most of the liquid, then drain the pork and pat it dry. Remove the chili.
Heat 1 inch of oil to 350°F. Fry the pork in batches for 4 to 6 minutes, until deep golden and crisp at the edges.
Drain and serve hot with pikliz, fried plantains and rice, with a squeeze of sour orange on top.
haitian-griot.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Braising first, then frying, gives griot its tender center and crackly edges.
Dry the pork well before frying; wet meat spatters and won't crisp.
Keep the Scotch bonnet whole for flavor with gentle heat; slit it if you like it fiery.
haitian-griot.make_ahead: Marinate and braise up to 2 days ahead, then fry just before serving.
variations: Air fryer: toss the braised pork with a little oil and air-fry at 400°F for 12 to 15 minutes, shaking twice.

larb.title: Larb (Thai Minced Pork Salad)
larb.description: The bright, punchy salad of northeastern Thailand and Laos: minced pork dressed with lime, fish sauce and chili, tossed with fresh herbs and nutty toasted rice powder.

ingredients.item: uncooked sticky or jasmine rice, for toasted rice powder
sticky rice, lettuce cups, cucumber and long beans, to serve

steps: Toast the rice in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring constantly, for 10 to 15 minutes, until deep golden and smelling like popcorn. Cool and grind to a coarse powder.
Cook the pork with the water in a pan over medium heat, breaking it up, for 5 to 7 minutes, just until no longer pink. Don't brown it; it should stay moist.
Take the pan off the heat. Stir in the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar and chili flakes. Taste: it should be sour, salty and spicy all at once.
Add the shallots, green onions, most of the herbs and 2 tbsp of the toasted rice powder and toss.
Pile onto a plate, sprinkle with the rest of the herbs and rice powder, and serve with sticky rice and crisp vegetables to scoop it up.
larb.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Cooking the pork gently in a little water keeps it tender and juicy; larb isn't meant to be browned and crispy.
Season off the heat so the lime stays bright and fresh.
Toasted rice powder is essential: it adds a nutty crunch and soaks up the juices.
larb.make_ahead: The toasted rice powder keeps 2 months in a sealed jar. Larb is best eaten right after mixing.
variations: Larb gai: make it with ground chicken instead of pork.

mantu.title: Mantu (Afghan Dumplings)
mantu.description: Steamed dumplings filled with spiced beef and onion, served on cool garlic yogurt and topped with a warm tomato and split pea sauce and dried mint.

ingredients.item: all-purpose flour, plus more for rolling

steps: Mix the flour, salt and water into a firm dough. Knead 5 minutes, cover and rest 30 minutes.
Mix the beef, half the onion, coriander, pepper and salt for the filling.

Simmer the split peas in water for 30 minutes until tender, then drain. In the oil, soften the rest of the onion, add the garlic, tomato paste, tomato and paprika and a cup of water, then the split peas. Simmer 10 minutes into a thick sauce.
Roll the dough very thin and cut into 3 1/2-inch squares. Put a spoon of filling in each, bring two opposite corners together, then pinch the other two corners up to seal.
Steam the dumplings on oiled steamer racks for 25 to 30 minutes, until the filling is cooked and the wrappers are translucent.
Stir the grated garlic and a pinch of salt into the yogurt. Spread half on a platter, arrange the mantu on top, spoon over the tomato sauce and remaining yogurt, and finish with dried mint.
mantu.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Roll the dough as thin as you can; thick wrappers turn doughy when steamed.
Raw onion in the filling releases juice as it steams, keeping the meat moist.
The cool yogurt, warm sauce and dried mint together are what make mantu, so don't skip any of them.
mantu.make_ahead: Freeze shaped, uncooked dumplings on a tray, then bag them; steam from frozen for 35 minutes. Both sauces keep 3 days.
variations: Shortcut: use store-bought round dumpling or wonton wrappers.

ropa-vieja.title: Ropa Vieja (Cuban Shredded Beef)
ropa-vieja.description: Cuba's national dish: flank steak braised until it falls into strands, then simmered in a sofrito of peppers, onion, tomato, cumin and olives. Serve with rice, black beans and sweet plantains.

ingredients.item: green bell pepper, sliced into strips
red bell pepper, sliced into strips
white rice, black beans and fried sweet plantains, to serve

steps: Put the steak, bay leaf, halved onion and salt in a pot and cover with water. Simmer, partly covered, for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, until very tender. Cool slightly in the liquid, then shred along the grain with two forks. Keep 1 cup of the broth.
In a wide pan, cook the sliced onion and peppers in the olive oil for 8 to 10 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic, cumin and oregano and stir for 1 minute.
Add the wine and let it bubble for 2 minutes, then the tomato sauce, reserved broth, shredded beef, olives and capers.
Simmer, uncovered, for 20 to 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce is thick and clings to the beef. Taste for salt.
Serve with white rice, black beans and fried sweet plantains.
ropa-vieja.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Flank steak's long fibers are what give ropa vieja its "old clothes" strands. Shred along the grain, not across it.
Letting the beef cool in its broth keeps it juicy.
Simmering the shredded beef in the sauce at the end lets it soak up all the flavor.
ropa-vieja.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge and tastes even better the next day. Freezes well for 3 months.
variations: Pressure cooker: cook the steak for 45 minutes on high, then finish in the sofrito as written.

caldo-verde.title: Caldo Verde (Portuguese Kale Soup)
caldo-verde.description: Portugal's beloved green soup: a velvety potato and onion broth, finished with ribbons of collard greens or kale and slices of smoky chouriço, with a ribbon of good olive oil on top.

ingredients.item: extra-virgin olive oil, plus more to serve
Portuguese chouriço or linguiça, thinly sliced
floury potatoes (Yukon Gold or russet), peeled and cut in chunks
collard greens or lacinato kale, stems removed
black pepper and crusty cornbread (broa), to serve

steps: Warm the olive oil in a large pot and fry the chouriço for 3 to 4 minutes, until lightly browned. Lift it out, leaving the paprika-red oil behind.
Cook the onion in the same oil for 6 to 8 minutes, until soft, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the potatoes, water and salt. Bring to a boil and simmer, partly covered, for 20 minutes, until the potatoes fall apart.
Meanwhile, stack the greens, roll them up tightly like a cigar and slice as thinly as you can into fine ribbons.
Blend the soup until smooth, right in the pot with a stick blender. It should be creamy but pourable; add water if it's too thick.
Bring back to a simmer, add the greens and cook 3 to 5 minutes, until bright green and just tender. Taste for salt.
Ladle into bowls, top with the chouriço and a thin drizzle of olive oil, and serve with cornbread.
caldo-verde.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Slice the greens as thin as angel hair. That fine chiffonade is what makes caldo verde: it cooks in minutes and stays bright green.
Don't add too much water at the start. You can thin the purée later, but a watery soup is hard to fix.
Add the greens only at the end so they keep their color and a little bite.
caldo-verde.make_ahead: The potato base keeps 3 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen. Add freshly cut greens and the sausage when reheating.
variations: Use Spanish chorizo or a smoked kielbasa if you can't find Portuguese sausage.

cou-cou-and-flying-fish.title: Cou-Cou and Flying Fish
cou-cou-and-flying-fish.description: The national dish of Barbados: lime-marinated flying fish steamed in a tomato, onion and pepper creole sauce, served over cou-cou, a smooth, buttery cornmeal and okra mash.

ingredients.item: flying fish fillets, or 1 1/2 lb thin white fish fillets
Bajan seasoning (green onion, thyme, parsley, garlic and hot pepper blended)
hot pepper sauce, plus more to serve
fine yellow cornmeal, soaked in 1 1/2 cups cold water

steps: Rub the fish with lime juice and a pinch of salt, rinse, then coat with the Bajan seasoning. Marinate 30 minutes or up to overnight.
Make the sauce: melt the butter and cook the onion and pepper for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, tomatoes, tomato paste, thyme, stock, hot sauce and 1/2 tsp salt, and simmer 10 minutes.
Lay the fish in the sauce, roll it up if it's thin, cover and steam gently for 8 to 10 minutes, until it flakes.
Meanwhile, make the cou-cou: boil the okra in the 4 cups water with 1 tsp salt for 5 minutes. Scoop out the okra and keep the slimy cooking water.

Over low heat, stir the soaked cornmeal into half the okra water, then keep adding the rest a ladle at a time, stirring hard with a wooden spoon, for 10 to 12 minutes, until thick, smooth and pulling away from the pan.
Stir in the okra and butter. Press the cou-cou into a buttered bowl, then turn it out onto a plate.
Make a well in the top and spoon over the fish and plenty of sauce. Serve with extra pepper sauce and lime.
cou-cou-and-flying-fish.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: The okra water is the secret: its natural thickness makes the cou-cou silky. Bajans stir it with a flat "cou-cou stick" to keep it lump-free.
Soaking the cornmeal in cold water first stops it from clumping when it hits the hot liquid.
Flying fish is delicate. Steam it gently in the sauce rather than boiling it.
cou-cou-and-flying-fish.make_ahead: The sauce keeps 3 days; cook the fish in it fresh. Cou-cou firms up as it cools; slice and fry leftovers in butter.
variations: Fried flying fish: dip the seasoned fillets in flour, egg and breadcrumbs and fry until golden, then serve the sauce on the side.

cracked-conch.title: Cracked Conch
cracked-conch.description: The Bahamas' fish-fry favorite: conch pounded thin and tender, dipped in a seasoned egg and flour coating, and fried until golden. Served with lime, hot sauce and a tangy dip.

ingredients.item: limes, juiced, plus wedges to serve
mayonnaise mixed with 2 tbsp ketchup and hot sauce, for dipping
French fries, coleslaw or peas and rice, to serve

steps: Rinse the conch, rub it with the lime juice and trim off any tough orange skin.
Put each piece between sheets of plastic wrap and pound with a meat mallet until about 1/4 inch thick and noticeably softer. Cut large pieces in half.
Whisk the eggs and milk in one dish. In another, mix the flour, garlic powder, seasoned salt, cayenne, pepper and thyme.
