Heat 2 inches of oil to 350°F. Dip the conch in flour, then egg, then flour again, pressing the coating on.
Fry 2 or 3 pieces at a time for 2 to 3 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp. Don't overcook or the conch toughens.
Drain on a rack and serve hot with lime wedges, the dipping sauce and fries, slaw or peas and rice.
cracked-conch.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: The name comes from "cracking", or pounding, the conch. Skip it and the meat is rubbery; overdo it and it falls apart.
Fry quickly and hot. Conch only needs a couple of minutes once it's been pounded thin.
Frozen cleaned conch from seafood or Caribbean markets works well; thaw it in the fridge.
cracked-conch.make_ahead: Pound and coat the conch up to 2 hours ahead and chill on a tray; fry just before serving.
variations: Use thin calamari steaks or pounded shrimp if you can't find conch.

dan-dan-noodles.title: Dan Dan Noodles
dan-dan-noodles.description: Sichuan's famous street noodles: springy wheat noodles in a numbing, spicy sesame and chili oil sauce, topped with crisp savory pork, preserved mustard greens and crushed peanuts.

ingredients.item: sui mi ya cai (Sichuan preserved mustard greens)
hot noodle water or chicken broth
roasted peanuts, crushed, and sliced green onions, to serve

steps: Heat the oil in a wok and stir-fry the pork over medium-high heat for 5 to 7 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and slightly crisp.
Add the Shaoxing wine, sweet bean sauce and dark soy sauce and cook 1 minute. Push the pork aside, add the ya cai and stir for 30 seconds, then mix it in.
Whisk the sesame paste, light soy sauce, chili oil, vinegar, sugar, Sichuan pepper and garlic in a bowl, then loosen with the hot noodle water or broth.
Cook the noodles according to the package. Add the bok choy for the last minute, then drain.
Divide the sauce among four bowls, add the noodles and greens and top with the pork, peanuts and green onions. Toss everything together at the table.
dan-dan-noodles.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Fry the pork until it's dry and slightly crispy; that's what gives dan dan its savory crunch.
Toast the Sichuan peppercorns in a dry pan before grinding for the full tingling, numbing effect.
Toss well before eating: the sauce sits at the bottom of the bowl.
dan-dan-noodles.make_ahead: The pork topping and sauce keep 4 days in the fridge. Cook the noodles fresh.
variations: Use ground chicken or turkey instead of pork.

momos.title: Momos (Himalayan Dumplings)
momos.description: Juicy steamed dumplings from Nepal and Tibet, filled with spiced chicken, onion, ginger and cilantro, and served with a smoky roasted tomato and sesame achar.

ingredients.item: oil or melted butter, for the filling

steps: Mix the flour and water into a smooth, firm dough. Knead 5 minutes, cover and rest 30 minutes.
Mix the chicken, red onion, green onions, ginger, garlic, cilantro, cumin, coriander, turmeric, 1 tsp salt and oil. Chill while you make the achar.

Char the tomatoes and chilies in a dry pan or under the broiler until blackened in spots. Blend them with the toasted sesame, lime juice, timur, the rest of the salt and a little water into a thick sauce.
Roll the dough into a log, cut into 30 pieces and roll each into a thin 3 1/2-inch circle, thinner at the edges.
Put a spoon of filling in the center and pleat the edges together into a round purse, twisting the top to seal.
Steam on oiled racks for 10 to 12 minutes, until the wrappers are glossy and the filling is cooked through. Serve hot with the achar.
momos.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Roll the wrapper edges thinner than the center, so the pleated top isn't doughy.
The oil in the filling and the juice from the onion make the momos burst with broth when you bite them.
Charring the tomatoes gives the achar its smoky depth; don't skip it.
momos.make_ahead: Freeze shaped momos on a tray, then bag them; steam from frozen for 15 minutes. The achar keeps 5 days.
variations: Jhol momo: thin the achar with hot broth and serve the momos in it as a soup.
Kothey momo: pan-fry the bottoms in oil after steaming until crisp.

nasi-lemak.title: Nasi Lemak
nasi-lemak.description: Malaysia's national dish: fragrant coconut and pandan rice served with a sweet-spicy sambal, crispy fried anchovies, roasted peanuts, a boiled egg and fresh cucumber.

ingredients.item: pandan leaves, tied in a knot
dried red chilies, soaked and seeded
dried anchovies (ikan bilis), rinsed and dried

steps: Put the rice, coconut milk, water, pandan, ginger and salt in a pot or rice cooker. Cook as you would plain rice, then rest 10 minutes and fluff.
Blend the chilies, shallots, garlic and belacan into a paste with a splash of water.
Fry the anchovies in 1/4 cup oil until crisp, about 3 minutes, then the peanuts for 2 to 3 minutes until golden. Drain both.

In the same oil, fry the chili paste over medium-low heat for 10 to 15 minutes, stirring, until dark red and the oil separates. Add the onion rings, tamarind water and sugar and simmer 5 minutes. Stir in a third of the anchovies.
Mound the rice on plates and serve with sambal, anchovies, peanuts, egg and cucumber around it.
nasi-lemak.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Cook the sambal paste slowly until the oil splits away. Rushing it leaves a raw, harsh chili taste.
Fry the anchovies and peanuts separately; they cook at different speeds.
Serve on a banana leaf for the classic aroma.
nasi-lemak.make_ahead: The sambal keeps 2 weeks in the fridge and freezes well. Store the fried anchovies and peanuts airtight for 1 week.
variations: Add fried chicken (ayam goreng) or a squid sambal for a bigger meal.

nigerian-pepper-soup.title: Nigerian Goat Meat Pepper Soup
nigerian-pepper-soup.description: A fiery, aromatic broth from southern Nigeria: tender goat meat simmered with Scotch bonnet and the warm, earthy pepper soup spice blend, finished with fresh herbs.

ingredients.item: bone-in goat meat, cut into chunks
pepper soup spice (ehuru, uda, uziza blend)
uziza, utazi or scent leaves (or basil), chopped
boiled yam, plantain or rice, to serve

steps: Put the goat meat in a pot with the onion, half the peppers, the stock cubes, ginger and salt. Cover and let it steam in its own juices over medium heat for 10 minutes, stirring once.
Add the water, bring to a boil, then simmer, partly covered, for 1 to 1 1/4 hours, until the goat is tender.
Stir in the pepper soup spice, crayfish and the rest of the peppers and simmer 10 minutes more.
Add the leaves, simmer 2 minutes and taste for salt and heat. Serve hot in bowls, with yam, plantain or rice.
nigerian-pepper-soup.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Steaming the meat with the seasonings before adding water drives the flavor deep into it.
Pepper soup spice is sold ready-ground in African markets. A mix of ground nutmeg, cumin, coriander and black pepper is a rough stand-in.
It should be thin, clear and fiery, not thick like a stew.
nigerian-pepper-soup.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen. Add fresh leaves when reheating.
variations: Catfish pepper soup: use catfish steaks and simmer only 15 minutes so they don't fall apart.
Use bone-in chicken thighs and simmer 35 minutes.

pasta-alla-norma.title: Pasta alla Norma
pasta-alla-norma.description: Catania's famous pasta: silky fried eggplant in a garlicky tomato and basil sauce, finished with a snowfall of salty ricotta salata.

ingredients.item: medium eggplants (about 2 lb), cut into 1-inch cubes
salt, plus more for the pasta water
olive oil, for frying, plus 2 tbsp
whole peeled tomatoes, crushed by hand

steps: Toss the eggplant with 1 tsp salt and let it drain in a colander for 30 minutes. Pat very dry.
Fry the eggplant in the 1/2 cup oil in batches over medium-high heat for 6 to 8 minutes, until deep golden and creamy inside. Drain on paper towels.
In a clean pan, warm the 2 tbsp oil with the garlic and chili flakes until the garlic is pale gold. Add the tomatoes, 1/2 tsp salt and a few basil leaves. Simmer 15 minutes, until thickened.
Cook the pasta in well-salted water until al dente. Save a cup of the cooking water.
Stir two-thirds of the eggplant into the sauce, then toss in the pasta with a splash of pasta water.
Serve topped with the rest of the eggplant, torn basil and plenty of ricotta salata.
pasta-alla-norma.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Salting the eggplant draws out water, so it fries up creamy instead of soaking up oil.
Ricotta salata is firm, salty and crumbly, nothing like fresh ricotta. Mild feta or pecorino is the best substitute.
Keep some eggplant aside for the top so it stays a little crisp.
pasta-alla-norma.make_ahead: The sauce keeps 4 days. Fried eggplant can be made a day ahead and warmed in the oven.
variations: Lighter: roast the oiled eggplant at 425°F for 25 to 30 minutes instead of frying.

romanian-tripe-soup.title: Ciorbă de Burtă (Romanian Tripe Soup)
romanian-tripe-soup.description: Romania's beloved sour soup: tender strips of beef tripe in a rich broth, made silky with sour cream and egg yolk, and sharpened with vinegar and garlic. Served with hot peppers.

ingredients.item: celery root, peeled, or 2 celery stalks
garlic, crushed to a paste with a pinch of salt
white wine vinegar, plus more to taste
hot peppers and extra sour cream, to serve

steps: Rinse the tripe well, cover with cold water, boil 10 minutes, then drain and rinse. This removes strong odors.
Put the tripe, bones, bay leaves and 12 cups water in a large pot. Simmer gently, skimming often, for 2 1/2 to 3 hours, until the tripe is very tender.
Add the carrots, parsnip, celery root and onion for the last 45 minutes.
Lift out the tripe and vegetables. Strain the broth. Slice the tripe into thin strips and the carrot into matchsticks, and return them to the broth with the salt.
Whisk the sour cream and egg yolks in a bowl. Slowly whisk in 2 ladles of hot broth, then stir the mixture back into the pot over low heat. Don't let it boil.
Stir in half the garlic paste and the vinegar. Taste and add more vinegar or salt until it's pleasantly sour. Serve with hot peppers, more garlic and sour cream on the side.
romanian-tripe-soup.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Temper the egg yolks with hot broth before adding them to the pot, and never boil afterward, or they'll curdle.
The soup should taste clearly sour. Add vinegar a spoonful at a time and taste as you go.
Cleaned, pre-cooked tripe from the butcher cuts the simmering time to about 1 1/2 hours.
romanian-tripe-soup.make_ahead: The tripe and broth keep 4 days before adding the sour cream mixture. Reheat gently once thickened.
variations: Ciorbă de ciocănele: make it with pork shanks instead of tripe.

uzbek-plov.title: Uzbek Plov
uzbek-plov.description: Uzbekistan's national dish: rice steamed over a rich base of browned lamb, sweet carrots, onion and cumin, crowned with whole heads of soft, sweet garlic.

ingredients.item: large onions, sliced into half moons
yellow and orange carrots, cut into thick matchsticks
garlic, loose outer skin removed, left whole
medium-grain or basmati rice, rinsed until clear and soaked 30 minutes
sliced tomato and onion salad (achichuk), to serve

steps: Heat the oil in a heavy wide pot or Dutch oven until very hot. Brown the lamb in batches for 6 to 8 minutes, until deeply colored.
Add the onions and cook 5 to 8 minutes until golden, then the carrots. Cook 10 minutes without much stirring, until the carrots soften.
Make the zirvak: add half the cumin, the coriander, barberries, chili, 2 tsp salt, chickpeas and enough boiling water to just cover. Simmer, covered, for 40 minutes.
Drain the rice and spread it evenly over the zirvak. Don't stir. Pour boiling water gently over a spoon to come 1/2 inch above the rice. Add the remaining salt and cumin.
Boil, uncovered, until the water drops below the rice surface. Push the garlic heads into the rice, then gather the rice into a dome and poke 6 holes down to the bottom.
Cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 25 to 30 minutes, until the rice is tender. Rest 10 minutes.
Mix gently, mound on a platter with the meat and carrots on top and the garlic heads in the center. Serve with a fresh tomato and onion salad.
uzbek-plov.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Never stir once the rice goes on. The rice steams in layers above the zirvak and soaks up its flavor.
Cut the carrots by hand into thick matchsticks; grated carrots turn to mush.
Squeeze the soft, sweet garlic cloves onto your rice as you eat.
uzbek-plov.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge. Reheat with a splash of water, covered, so it steams.
variations: Use beef chuck instead of lamb; the timing is the same.
Add a handful of quince or dried apricots to the zirvak for a sweeter plov.

bigos.title: Bigos (Polish Hunter's Stew)
bigos.description: Poland's slow-cooked hunter's stew: sauerkraut and fresh cabbage braised with smoked kielbasa, pork, wild mushrooms, prunes and red wine until rich, tangy and deeply savory.

ingredients.item: pork shoulder, cut into bite-size pieces
salt and plenty of black pepper
rye bread or boiled potatoes, to serve

steps: Soak the porcini in the boiling water for 20 minutes. Lift them out, chop them, and keep the soaking liquid, leaving any grit behind.
In a large heavy pot, cook the bacon until crisp. Brown the pork in the fat for 6 to 8 minutes, then the kielbasa for 3 minutes. Lift everything out.
Cook the onion in the same pot for 5 minutes. Add the cabbage and cook 10 minutes until it wilts.
Add the sauerkraut, meats, mushrooms and their liquid, prunes, wine, tomato paste and all the spices. Stir well.
Cover and simmer very gently for 2 hours, stirring now and then and adding a splash of water if it gets dry. It should be thick, glossy and brown.
Taste and balance: add a splash of sauerkraut juice if it's too sweet, or a pinch of sugar if too sour. Serve with rye bread or potatoes.
bigos.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Bigos is famously better on the second and third day. Many Polish cooks reheat it for several days in a row before serving.
Taste the sauerkraut first. If it's very sour, rinse it once before using.
The dried porcini and prunes give bigos its deep, smoky-sweet flavor; don't leave them out.
bigos.make_ahead: Keeps 5 days in the fridge and freezes for 3 months; the flavor improves each time it's reheated.
variations: Add leftover roast meats such as beef, venison or duck, as hunters once did.

chicken-paprikash.title: Chicken Paprikash (Paprikás Csirke)
chicken-paprikash.description: Hungary's comfort classic: bone-in chicken braised in a velvety sauce of onions, sweet Hungarian paprika and sour cream, served over little egg dumplings (nokedli).

ingredients.item: bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and drumsticks
Hungarian wax or bell pepper, chopped
full-fat sour cream, at room temperature

steps: Season the chicken with 1 tsp salt. Brown it skin-side down in the lard in a wide pot for 5 to 6 minutes, then turn for 2 minutes. Lift out.
Cook the onions in the fat for 10 minutes until soft and golden. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the paprika, so it doesn't burn. Add the pepper, tomato, broth and the rest of the salt, then return the chicken.
Cover and simmer gently for 30 to 35 minutes, until the chicken is tender.

Meanwhile, make the nokedli: mix the flour, eggs, water and a pinch of salt into a thick, sticky batter. Scrape small bits into simmering salted water with a spoon or spaetzle maker. When they float, cook 1 minute more, drain and toss with butter.
Whisk the sour cream and 1 tbsp flour, then whisk in a ladle of the hot sauce. Stir it into the pot and simmer gently 2 to 3 minutes until thickened. Serve over the nokedli.
chicken-paprikash.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Always add paprika off the heat. Scorched paprika turns bitter in seconds.
Real Hungarian sweet paprika makes the biggest difference; it's richer and redder than generic paprika.
Temper the sour cream with hot sauce first so it doesn't split.
chicken-paprikash.make_ahead: The braise keeps 3 days; stir in the sour cream when reheating. Nokedli can be made a day ahead and warmed in butter.
variations: Serve with egg noodles, rice or mashed potatoes instead of nokedli.
Add 1/2 tsp hot paprika for a spicier version.

chicken-yassa.title: Chicken Yassa
chicken-yassa.description: Senegal's beloved braise: chicken marinated in lemon, mustard and garlic, grilled, then simmered with a mountain of slowly caramelized onions, olives and a whole hot pepper.

ingredients.item: Scotch bonnet chili, left whole and pricked
white or broken rice, to serve

steps: Whisk the lemon juice, 2 tbsp mustard, garlic, vinegar, half the oil, salt and pepper. Toss the chicken and onions in it and marinate at least 3 hours, or overnight.
Lift the chicken out, shaking off the onions, and grill or broil it for 5 to 6 minutes a side, until well browned. It doesn't need to be cooked through.
Lift the onions from the marinade (keep the liquid). Cook them in the remaining oil in a wide pot over medium heat for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring often, until soft and golden.
Add the marinade, remaining mustard, chili, bay leaf, stock cube and water. Nestle in the chicken.
Cover and simmer gently for 30 minutes, until the chicken is tender. Add the olives for the last 5 minutes. Serve over rice with plenty of onion sauce.
chicken-yassa.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: The onions are the star. Give them time to soften and turn sweet before the chicken goes back in.
Grilling the chicken first adds a smoky char, the way it's done in Senegal.
Keep the chili whole for flavor and gentle heat; break it open if you like it fiery.
chicken-yassa.make_ahead: Marinate up to a day ahead. The finished dish keeps 4 days and tastes even better reheated.
variations: Yassa poisson: use thick fish steaks and simmer only 10 minutes.

finnish-salmon-soup.title: Lohikeitto (Finnish Salmon Soup)
finnish-salmon-soup.description: Finland's comforting salmon soup: tender chunks of salmon, potatoes, carrot and leek in a light, creamy broth, scented with allspice and lots of fresh dill.

ingredients.item: skinless salmon fillet, cut into 1-inch chunks
leek, white and light green parts, sliced
waxy potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
salt and white pepper, to taste
rye bread and butter, to serve

steps: Melt the butter in a pot and soften the leek for 5 minutes without browning.
Add the potatoes, carrots, stock, bay leaf, allspice and salt. Simmer 15 minutes, until the potatoes are just tender.
Turn the heat to low. Add the cream, salmon and most of the dill.
Cook very gently for 4 to 5 minutes, without boiling, until the salmon just turns opaque. Season with pepper and serve with the rest of the dill and rye bread.
finnish-salmon-soup.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Add the salmon at the end and keep the soup below a boil, so the fish stays tender and the cream doesn't split.
Fresh dill is essential; dried dill doesn't come close.
Use the salmon skin and trimmings to make a quick stock for extra flavor.
finnish-salmon-soup.make_ahead: Best eaten fresh. Leftovers keep 2 days; reheat gently without boiling.
variations: Lighter: use half whole milk and half cream.

imam-bayildi.title: Imam Bayildi (Turkish Stuffed Eggplant)
imam-bayildi.description: A classic Turkish olive oil dish: whole eggplants fried until silky, split and stuffed with sweet onions, tomatoes, peppers and garlic, then baked until meltingly soft. Best at room temperature.

ingredients.item: salt, plus more for the eggplants
green peppers (Turkish sivri or Anaheim), chopped
ripe tomatoes, grated or finely chopped

steps: Peel the eggplants in lengthwise stripes, leaving stripes of skin on. Soak them in salted water for 20 minutes, then pat very dry.
Fry the eggplants whole in 1/3 cup oil, turning, for 10 to 12 minutes, until golden and soft. Lay them in a baking dish.

In the same pan, cook the onions in the rest of the oil for 10 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and peppers for 3 minutes, then the tomatoes, tomato paste, sugar and salt. Cook 5 minutes, then stir in the parsley.
Split each eggplant down the middle without cutting through, and gently open it into a pocket. Fill generously with the onion mixture.
Mix the hot water and lemon juice and pour around the eggplants. Cover with foil and bake at 350°F for 40 minutes, until very tender.
Cool to room temperature before serving, drizzled with the pan juices.
imam-bayildi.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Don't skimp on the olive oil. This is a zeytinyağlı dish: the oil carries all the flavor.
Imam bayildi tastes best the next day, served at room temperature.
Striping the skin helps the eggplant hold its shape while letting it soften evenly.
imam-bayildi.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge. Bring to room temperature before serving.
variations: Lighter: roast the oiled eggplants at 425°F for 30 minutes instead of frying.
Karnıyarık: add browned ground beef to the filling for the meaty version.

katsudon.title: Katsudon
katsudon.description: Japan's comforting rice bowl: a crisp panko pork cutlet simmered briefly with sweet onions in dashi, soy and mirin, then softly set with egg and served over steamed rice.

ingredients.item: boneless pork loin chops (about 5 oz each), 1/2 inch thick
salt and a pinch of pepper

steps: Make a few small cuts in the fat around each chop so it stays flat. Season, then coat in flour, beaten egg and panko.
Fry in 1/2 inch of oil at 340°F for 3 to 4 minutes a side, until golden and cooked through. Drain on a rack and slice into strips.
In a small frying pan, simmer the dashi, soy sauce, mirin and sugar with the onion for 3 to 4 minutes, until the onion is soft.
Lay one sliced cutlet on the onions. Pour half the beaten eggs around and over it, cover and cook 1 minute, until the egg is just barely set.
Slide it over a bowl of rice and top with green onion. Repeat for the second bowl.
katsudon.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Beat the eggs only lightly so you can still see streaks of white and yolk. That marbled look is the classic finish.
Pour the egg around the cutlet, not all over it, so part of the crust stays crisp.
Leftover tonkatsu is perfect here; the sauce brings it back to life.
katsudon.make_ahead: Fry the cutlets up to a day ahead and reheat in the oven. Cook the egg topping just before serving.
variations: Oyakodon: use sliced chicken thigh simmered in the sauce instead of the pork cutlet.

mangu.title: Mangú con los Tres Golpes
mangu.description: The Dominican Republic's favorite breakfast: buttery mashed green plantains topped with vinegary red onions, served with the "three hits": fried salami, fried cheese and fried eggs.

ingredients.item: green (unripe) plantains, peeled and cut in chunks
cold water, from the plantain pot
large red onion, sliced into rings
queso de freír (frying cheese), sliced 1/2 inch thick

steps: Boil the plantains in salted water for 15 to 20 minutes, until very tender.
Meanwhile, cook the onion rings in the olive oil for 3 minutes, add the vinegar and a pinch of salt and cook 2 minutes more, until just softened and tangy.
Drain the plantains, keeping some of the water. Mash them with the butter, adding cold water a little at a time, until smooth and creamy.
Fry the salami slices in a little oil for 2 minutes a side until crisp at the edges. Fry the cheese in the same pan for 1 to 2 minutes a side until golden.
Fry the eggs sunny side up.
Pile the mangú on plates, top with the onions and their juices, and serve with the salami, cheese, eggs and avocado.
mangu.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Mash the plantains while they're hot and add the water cold. Dominican cooks swear it makes the mangú extra smooth.
Use fully green plantains; ripe ones make a sweet, different dish.
Pat the cheese dry before frying so it browns instead of spattering.
mangu.make_ahead: Mangú stiffens as it cools; reheat with a splash of water and stir until smooth.
variations: Use queso blanco or halloumi if you can't find queso de freír.

mohinga.title: Mohinga (Burmese Fish Noodle Soup)
mohinga.description: Myanmar's national breakfast: thin rice noodles in a thick, golden catfish broth fragrant with lemongrass, ginger and turmeric, thickened with toasted rice and chickpea flour. Topped with egg, fritters, lime and chili.

ingredients.item: lemongrass, bruised, plus 1 stalk finely chopped
rice flour, toasted in a dry pan until golden
chickpea flour, toasted in a dry pan until golden
small shallots, peeled and left whole
sliced banana stem or banana blossom (optional)
cilantro, lime wedges, chili flakes, fried onions and split pea fritters, to serve

steps: Simmer the catfish in the water with the bruised lemongrass, sliced ginger, 1 tsp turmeric and 1 tbsp fish sauce for 15 minutes. Lift out the fish and flake it. Strain and keep the broth.

In a large pot, fry the onions in the oil for 8 minutes until golden. Add the garlic, grated ginger, chopped lemongrass, shrimp paste, paprika, chili flakes and the rest of the turmeric for 2 minutes.
Add the flaked fish and stir for 2 minutes. Pour in the broth.
Whisk the toasted rice flour and chickpea flour with a cup of water until smooth, then stir into the pot. Add the shallots and banana stem.
Simmer 30 minutes, stirring often, until thickened and the shallots are soft. Season with the remaining fish sauce.
Put noodles in each bowl, ladle the soup over and top with egg, cilantro, lime, chili and crunchy fritters or fried onions.
mohinga.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Toast the rice flour and chickpea flour until nutty and golden; this gives the broth its body and flavor.
Whisk the flours into cold water before adding them, so the soup stays smooth.
The crunchy toppings matter as much as the soup. Don't skip the fritters or fried onions.
mohinga.make_ahead: The broth keeps 3 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen. Cook the noodles fresh.
variations: Use canned mackerel or sardines, a favorite shortcut in Burmese homes abroad.

samgyetang.title: Samgyetang (Korean Ginseng Chicken Soup)
samgyetang.description: Korea's restorative summer soup: a whole small chicken stuffed with sweet rice, ginseng, jujubes and garlic, simmered until falling-off-the-bone tender in a milky broth.

ingredients.item: fresh ginseng roots (or 2 tbsp dried ginseng)
salt and black pepper, at the table

steps: Rinse the hens inside and out and pat dry. Stuff each with soaked rice, 1 ginseng root, 1 jujube and 4 garlic cloves. Don't pack it too tightly.
Cross the legs and tie them, or tuck one leg through a small slit in the other, to keep the stuffing in.
Put the hens in a pot with the water, ginger, the rest of the garlic and jujubes, and any leftover rice.
Bring to a boil, skim, then simmer, covered, for 50 to 60 minutes, until the meat pulls easily from the bone and the rice is soft.
Serve each hen in a large bowl of broth, scattered with green onion. Season with salt and pepper at the table and eat with kimchi.
samgyetang.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Leave room for the rice to swell or it will burst out of the hen.
Samgyetang is seasoned by each diner at the table, so the broth is cooked without salt.
Look for samgyetang kits at Korean markets; they bundle the rice, jujubes and dried ginseng.
samgyetang.make_ahead: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat gently. Leftover broth makes a lovely rice porridge.
variations: Use a 3-lb whole chicken for 4 people and simmer 1 hour 15 minutes.

tortilla-espanola.title: Tortilla Española (Spanish Omelette)
tortilla-espanola.description: Spain's beloved tapa: thin slices of potato and onion slowly poached in olive oil, folded into beaten eggs and cooked into a thick, golden cake with a soft, juicy center.

ingredients.item: Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced

steps: Heat the oil in a 10-inch nonstick skillet over medium-low heat. Add the potatoes, onion and 1 tsp salt. The oil should almost cover them.
Cook gently for 20 to 25 minutes, turning now and then, until the potatoes are completely tender but not browned.
Drain the potatoes and onion in a colander set over a bowl, keeping the oil. Beat the eggs with the rest of the salt in a large bowl, then fold in the warm potatoes. Rest 10 minutes.
Wipe the pan, heat 2 tbsp of the reserved oil over medium heat and pour in the mixture. Cook 4 to 5 minutes, shaking the pan and tucking in the edges, until the bottom is golden.
Put a large plate over the pan and flip the tortilla onto it in one confident move. Slide it back into the pan and cook 2 to 3 minutes more.
Slide onto a plate and rest 5 minutes. Serve warm or at room temperature, cut in wedges.
tortilla-espanola.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: The potatoes should poach, not fry. Keep the heat low so they turn soft and creamy.
Resting the potatoes in the egg lets them soak it up for a juicy, cohesive tortilla.
Strain and keep the potato oil; it's wonderful for cooking.
tortilla-espanola.make_ahead: Keeps 2 days in the fridge. Many Spaniards prefer it the next day, at room temperature.
variations: Leave the center runny (poco hecha) for the classic bar-style tortilla.
Add sliced chorizo or roasted peppers to the eggs.

amaretto-sour.title: Amaretto Sour
amaretto-sour.description: The modern amaretto sour: a nut-free, almond-flavored amaretto balanced with fresh lemon and a splash of strong bourbon, shaken with egg white for a silky foam. Sweet, rich and bright.
steps: Shake the amaretto, bourbon, lemon juice, syrup and egg white without ice for 15 seconds to build the foam.
Add ice and shake hard for 10 seconds more.
Strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice. Garnish with an orange slice and cherry, and dot the foam with bitters.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake orgeat, lemon juice, cold black tea and aquafaba for an almond sour mocktail.

amaretto-sour.note: Uses raw egg white; use pasteurized egg white if you prefer.
tips: The splash of high-proof bourbon is what keeps this drink from tasting like candy.
The dry shake (no ice) whips the egg white into a thick, creamy head.
variations: Use regular-proof bourbon and increase it to 1 oz if you don't have cask strength.

barracuda.title: Barracuda
barracuda.description: A sunny Italian classic from the 1960s: gold rum, vanilla-herbal Galliano, pineapple and lime, shaken and topped with a splash of Prosecco.

ingredients.item: vegan prosecco (such as Mionetto Organic), chilled

steps: Shake the rum, Galliano, pineapple juice and lime with ice until very cold.
Strain into a chilled coupe or margarita glass.
Top with the Prosecco and garnish with a pineapple wedge.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake pineapple juice, lime and a little vanilla syrup, then top with sparkling white grape juice.

barracuda.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Galliano's vanilla and anise notes are the heart of the drink; there isn't a close substitute.
Shaking pineapple juice gives the drink a lovely frothy head.
variations: Serve it in a hollowed-out pineapple for a party.

blue-moon.title: Blue Moon
blue-moon.description: A forgotten gin classic, close cousin of the Aviation: London dry gin and fresh lemon, softened and tinted pale lavender with floral crème de violette.
steps: Shake the gin, crème de violette and lemon juice with ice until very cold.
Fine strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
Express a lemon twist over the top and drop it in.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake lemon juice, a dash of violet syrup and cold sparkling water with ice and strain into a cocktail glass.

blue-moon.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Use a crisp London dry gin; soft gins get lost under the violet.
Crème de violette varies by brand. Start with 1/2 oz and add more if you want a deeper violet color and flavor.
variations: For a silkier version, add 1/2 oz egg white and dry shake first.

bourbon-smash.title: Bourbon Smash
bourbon-smash.description: A minty, citrusy cousin of the julep: lemon wedges muddled with mint and sugar, shaken hard with bourbon and served over crushed ice.
steps: Muddle the lemon wedges in a shaker to press out the juice and the oils from the peel.
Add the mint, syrup and bourbon, then fill with ice and shake hard.
Double strain into a rocks glass filled with crushed ice.
Garnish with a big sprig of mint, slapped between your hands to wake up the aroma.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Muddle lemon, mint and syrup, shake with cold green tea and serve over crushed ice.

bourbon-smash.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Muddling the lemon wedges, not just squeezing juice, adds bright peel oils; that's what makes a smash.
Press the mint gently in the shaker; shaking alone releases plenty of flavor.
variations: Peach smash: muddle two ripe peach slices with the lemon.
Use rye for a spicier smash.

brooklynite.title: Brooklynite
brooklynite.description: A honeyed daiquiri from the 1946 Stork Club Bar Book: funky Jamaican rum, fresh lime and honey syrup with a dash of bitters, served up.

ingredients.item: honey syrup (equal parts honey and hot water)

steps: Shake the rum, lime juice, honey syrup and bitters with ice until very cold.
Fine strain into a chilled coupe.
Garnish with a lime twist.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake lime juice, honey syrup, cold black tea and a dash of vanilla, and strain into a coupe.

brooklynite.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Thin the honey with hot water first so it mixes in instead of sticking to the ice.
A molasses-rich Jamaican rum gives this its deep, funky character.
variations: Swap in an aged rum for a smoother, rounder drink.

cantarito.title: Cantarito
cantarito.description: A Jalisco roadside favorite: tequila and fresh orange, grapefruit and lime juices with a pinch of salt, topped with grapefruit soda and served ice-cold in a clay cup.
steps: Soak a clay cantarito cup in cold water for 10 minutes, then pour out the water. Rim it with Tajín if you like.
Fill the cup with ice. Add the tequila, citrus juices and salt and stir.
Top with the grapefruit soda, stir gently and garnish with citrus wedges.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Mix the citrus juices and salt, top with grapefruit soda and serve in a chilled clay cup.

cantarito.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Soaking the clay cup keeps the drink extra cold as the water slowly evaporates.
A pinch of salt makes all the citrus taste brighter.
variations: Make a pitcher: multiply by 8 and add the soda just before serving.

caribou-lou.title: Caribou Lou
caribou-lou.description: A sweet, tropical party drink made famous by a 2006 Tech N9ne song: overproof rum and coconut rum over ice, filled with pineapple juice. Strong, so sip slowly.
steps: Fill a hurricane glass with ice.
Add the overproof rum, coconut rum and pineapple juice.
Stir well and garnish with a pineapple wedge.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Mix pineapple juice with a splash of coconut water and coconut syrup over ice.

caribou-lou.note: Overproof rum is flammable; keep it away from open flames.
tips: Overproof rum is very strong. For a milder drink, use regular white rum instead.
Shake it with ice instead of building it for a frothy top.
variations: Make it a punch: mix a bottle-sized batch in a jug and serve over ice.

chilcano.title: Chilcano
chilcano.description: Peru's favorite highball: pisco lengthened with ginger ale and fresh lime over ice, finished with a few drops of bitters. Light, spicy and refreshing.
steps: Fill a highball glass with ice and add the pisco and lime juice.
Top with ginger ale and stir gently.
Add the bitters on top and garnish with a lime wheel.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Pour lime juice over ice, top with ginger ale and add a few drops of bitters, or skip them for no alcohol at all.

chilcano.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Peruvian Quebranta pisco is traditional; any good pisco works.
Use a dry, spicy ginger ale rather than a sweet one.
variations: Chilcano de maracuyá: shake in 1 oz passion fruit pulp before topping with ginger ale.

cynar-julep.title: Cynar Julep
cynar-julep.description: Buenos Aires' favorite modern classic: bittersweet artichoke amaro with mint, lemon and grapefruit over crushed ice. Low in alcohol and very refreshing.
steps: Gently muddle the mint with the syrup and lemon juice in a julep cup or rocks glass.
Add the Cynar and fill with crushed ice. Swizzle with a spoon until the glass frosts.
Top with grapefruit juice or soda and more crushed ice. Garnish with a big mint sprig.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Muddle mint with syrup and lemon, then top with grapefruit juice, soda and crushed ice.

cynar-julep.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Cynar is bitter but not harsh; grapefruit and mint bring out its sweet, herbal side.
Swizzling over crushed ice chills and dilutes the drink quickly; that's what makes a julep.
variations: Add a splash of gin for a stronger version, as in the original Buenos Aires recipe.

death-flip.title: Death Flip
death-flip.description: A modern classic from Melbourne's Black Pearl bar: tequila, yellow Chartreuse and Jägermeister shaken with a whole egg into a rich, gingerbread-spiced flip.
steps: Shake the tequila, Chartreuse, Jägermeister, syrup and egg without ice for 15 seconds.
Add ice and shake hard for 10 seconds more.
Fine strain into a small chilled coupe or wine glass and grate nutmeg over the top.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake cold chai concentrate, a whole egg and a little vanilla syrup, and top with nutmeg.

death-flip.note: Uses a raw egg; use a pasteurized egg if you prefer.
tips: The dry shake emulsifies the whole egg into a light, airy texture rather than a heavy one.
Grate the nutmeg fresh; its aroma is a big part of the drink.

french-connection.title: French Connection
french-connection.description: A smooth 1970s after-dinner sipper: cognac and nut-free amaretto stirred over ice. Warm, almond-scented and simple.
steps: Fill a rocks glass with ice, ideally one large cube.
Add the cognac and amaretto and stir for 15 seconds.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Stir cold black tea with a splash of almond (orgeat) syrup over ice.

french-connection.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Adjust the amaretto to taste; use less for a drier drink.
A large ice cube melts slowly, keeping the drink strong and cold.
variations: Godfather: use Scotch instead of cognac.

harvey-wallbanger.title: Harvey Wallbanger
harvey-wallbanger.description: The 1970s disco-era favorite: a vodka and fresh orange juice highball with a float of golden, vanilla-anise Galliano on top.
steps: Fill a highball glass with ice and add the vodka and orange juice. Stir.
Slowly pour the Galliano over the back of a bar spoon so it floats on top.
Garnish with an orange slice and cherry.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Top orange juice with a splash of vanilla syrup over ice.

harvey-wallbanger.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Fresh-squeezed orange juice makes a huge difference here.
Float the Galliano last so the first sips are fragrant with vanilla.
variations: Freddy Fudpucker: use tequila instead of vodka.

hotel-georgia.title: Hotel Georgia
hotel-georgia.description: A 1940s classic from Vancouver's Hotel Georgia: gin, almond orgeat and lemon, shaken with egg white and perfumed with orange flower water.
steps: Shake the gin, orgeat, lemon juice, egg white and orange flower water without ice for 15 seconds.
Add ice and shake hard again.
Fine strain into a chilled coupe and grate a little nutmeg over the foam.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake orgeat, lemon, cold sparkling water and a drop of orange flower water with aquafaba.

hotel-georgia.note: Uses raw egg white; use pasteurized egg white if you prefer.
tips: Orange flower water is very strong; measure in dashes, not spoons.
Good orgeat makes the drink. Look for one made with real almonds.

kir.title: Kir
kir.description: The classic Burgundy aperitif: crisp, dry white wine blushed pink with a splash of blackcurrant liqueur (crème de cassis).

ingredients.item: vegan dry white wine (such as Bonterra Sauvignon Blanc), well chilled

steps: Pour the crème de cassis into a chilled white wine glass.
Top with the cold wine; it mixes as you pour.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Add a splash of blackcurrant syrup to chilled sparkling water or non-alcoholic white wine.

kir.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Keep the cassis light; the drink should be pale pink, not purple.
Both the wine and glass should be very cold.
variations: Kir Royale: use Champagne instead of white wine, served in a flute.
Kir Pétillant: use any dry sparkling wine.

madras.title: Madras
madras.description: A bright, easygoing highball: vodka over ice with cranberry juice and orange juice. Sweet-tart and pretty in red and orange.
steps: Fill a highball glass with ice and add the vodka and cranberry juice.
Pour the orange juice over the top for a sunset effect, or stir to blend.
Garnish with an orange slice.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Mix cranberry and orange juice over ice with a squeeze of lime.

madras.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Pour the orange juice last and gently for a layered look.
variations: Bay Breeze: use pineapple juice instead of orange juice.
Sea Breeze: use grapefruit juice instead of orange juice.

queen-elizabeth.title: Queen Elizabeth
queen-elizabeth.description: The brandy Queen Elizabeth from The Savoy Cocktail Book era: cognac and sweet vermouth with a touch of orange curaçao, stirred and served up with a cherry. Like a rich, orange-scented Manhattan.

ingredients.item: vegan sweet vermouth (such as Dolin Rouge)

steps: Stir the cognac, vermouth and curaçao with ice for 20 to 30 seconds, until very cold.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
Garnish with a brandied or maraschino cherry on a pick.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Stir cold black tea with a splash of non-alcoholic red vermouth and orange syrup, and garnish with a cherry.

queen-elizabeth.note: There is also a gin Queen Elizabeth (gin, dry vermouth and Bénédictine); this is the brandy version.
tips: Stir, don't shake; it keeps the drink clear and silky.
Use a fresh bottle of sweet vermouth, stored in the fridge once opened.
variations: Add 2 dashes of Angostura bitters for a drier, spicier drink.

raspberry-beret.title: Raspberry Beret
raspberry-beret.description: A ruby-red raspberry gin sour: fresh raspberries muddled with lemon and gin, shaken with raspberry liqueur and egg white into a silky pink foam.
steps: Muddle the raspberries in a shaker until completely crushed.
Add the gin, raspberry liqueur, lemon juice, syrup and egg white and shake without ice for 15 seconds.
Add ice and shake hard again.
Double strain into a chilled coupe and garnish with raspberries on a pick.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Muddle raspberries with lemon and syrup, shake with aquafaba and cold sparkling water, and strain into a coupe.

raspberry-beret.note: Uses raw egg white; use pasteurized egg white if you prefer.
tips: Double strain through a fine sieve to catch the raspberry seeds.
Ripe, in-season raspberries give the brightest color and flavor.
variations: Use vodka instead of gin for a softer drink.

saturn.title: Saturn
saturn.description: A 1967 award-winning tiki classic: gin with lemon, passion fruit, falernum and almond orgeat. Bright, tropical and floral, served up with a lemon twist.
steps: Shake the gin, lemon juice, passion fruit syrup, falernum and orgeat hard with ice.
Fine strain into a chilled coupe.
Garnish with a lemon twist curled around the rim, like the rings of Saturn.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake passion fruit syrup, lemon, a little orgeat and cold sparkling water with ice.

saturn.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: The tiki-bar version is flash-blended with crushed ice and served in a tall glass; shaken and served up, it's crisper.
A juniper-forward London dry gin holds up well against the tropical syrups.
variations: Flash blend with 1 cup crushed ice and serve in a pilsner glass with a lemon peel ring.

sherry-sangaree.title: Sherry Sangaree
sherry-sangaree.description: One of the oldest mixed drinks: rich oloroso sherry lightly sweetened, chilled and served with a dusting of nutmeg and a twist of lemon.

ingredients.item: vegan oloroso sherry (such as Barbadillo Oloroso Seco)

steps: Stir the sherry and syrup with ice until very cold.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
Grate nutmeg over the top and garnish with a lemon twist.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Stir cold black tea with a little prune or raisin syrup and top with nutmeg.

sherry-sangaree.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Oloroso is nutty and rich; amontillado gives a lighter, drier drink.
Fresh nutmeg is essential; its aroma is a big part of the drink.
variations: Port Sangaree: use ruby port instead of sherry.
Serve it long over ice with a splash of soda for a lighter aperitif.

spaghett.title: Spaghett
spaghett.description: A cult bar favorite: a cold bottle of light American lager, spiked with Aperol and fresh lemon right in the bottle. Bitter, bubbly and refreshing.

ingredients.item: vegan light lager (such as Miller High Life), ice-cold

steps: Drink or pour off about 2 oz of the beer to make room.
Add the Aperol and lemon juice straight into the bottle.
Tip gently once to mix and drink from the bottle.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Add a splash of non-alcoholic bitter orange aperitif and lemon to a non-alcoholic lager.

spaghett.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Start with 1 oz Aperol if you like it less bitter, and add more to taste.
Pour slowly to avoid it foaming over.
variations: Swap Campari for Aperol for a more bitter drink.

b-52.title: B-52
b-52.description: The famous layered shot: coffee liqueur, Irish cream and orange liqueur stacked in three neat stripes.
steps: Pour the coffee liqueur into a shot glass.
Slowly pour the Irish cream over the back of a bar spoon so it floats on top.
Float the Grand Marnier the same way to make the top layer.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Layer cold coffee syrup, a little cream and orange syrup in a shot glass.

b-52.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Pour very slowly over the back of a spoon held just above the last layer.
Chill the liqueurs first; cold layers stay separate more easily.
variations: Flaming B-52: light the top layer briefly, then extinguish before drinking. Be very careful.

cafe-brulot.title: Café Brûlot
cafe-brulot.description: New Orleans' flaming coffee: brandy and orange liqueur warmed with sugar, cinnamon, cloves and citrus peel, set alight, then mixed with hot dark coffee.

ingredients.item: orange, peel cut in one long strip
hot strong coffee (New Orleans chicory coffee is traditional)

steps: Put the citrus peels, cinnamon, cloves and sugar cubes in a heatproof bowl or small saucepan.
Add the brandy and curaçao and warm gently over low heat, stirring to dissolve the sugar. Don't let it boil.
Away from anything flammable, carefully light the warm brandy with a long match. Ladle it over the orange peel for a minute as it flames.
Slowly pour in the hot coffee to put out the flames. Stir and ladle into heatproof glasses, with a strip of peel in each.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Simmer coffee with orange peel, cinnamon, cloves and sugar, and serve hot.

cafe-brulot.note: Flaming alcohol is dangerous. Work slowly, keep a lid nearby to smother the flame, and never pour spirits from the bottle near a flame.
tips: Warm the brandy only gently; if it's too hot it may flare up suddenly.
Use heatproof glasses or mugs, and keep long hair and sleeves away from the flame.
variations: Stud the orange peel with the cloves for the classic restaurant presentation.

lynchburg-lemonade.title: Lynchburg Lemonade
lynchburg-lemonade.description: A Tennessee favorite: Tennessee whiskey, triple sec and fresh lemon, topped with lemon-lime soda over ice. Sweet, tangy and easy-drinking.
steps: Shake the whiskey, triple sec, lemon juice and syrup with ice.
Strain into a tall glass filled with ice.
Top with the lemon-lime soda, stir gently and garnish with a lemon wheel.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake lemon juice and syrup, then top with lemon-lime soda over ice.

lynchburg-lemonade.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Fresh lemon juice beats bottled sour mix every time.
Add the soda last and stir gently to keep the bubbles.
variations: Make a pitcher: multiply by 8 and top with soda just before serving.

miami-vice.title: Miami Vice
miami-vice.description: Two frozen favorites in one glass: a frozen strawberry daiquiri swirled with a frozen piña colada. Fruity, creamy and very tropical.
steps: Blend 1 oz rum with the strawberries, lime juice, syrup and 1 cup ice until smooth. Pour into a jug and rinse the blender.
Blend the other 1 oz rum with the cream of coconut, pineapple juice and 1 cup ice until smooth.
Pour the two mixtures into a tall glass at the same time, from opposite sides, so they swirl together.
Garnish with a pineapple wedge and a strawberry.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Make both blends without rum and swirl them together.

miami-vice.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Cream of coconut (sweetened, like Coco López) is not the same as coconut cream or coconut milk.
Keep each blend thick so they stay separate in the glass.
variations: Use dark rum in the piña colada half for a richer flavor.

st-germain-cocktail.title: St-Germain Cocktail
st-germain-cocktail.description: The elderflower spritz: floral St-Germain liqueur topped with dry sparkling wine and soda over ice, with a twist of lemon.

ingredients.item: vegan dry sparkling wine (such as Mionetto Organic Prosecco), chilled

steps: Pour the St-Germain into a chilled champagne flute.
Top with the sparkling wine, then the soda water.
Stir once gently and garnish with a lemon twist.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Mix elderflower cordial with sparkling water and a squeeze of lemon over ice.

st-germain-cocktail.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Pour the bubbles gently down the side of the glass so they stay lively.
Squeeze the lemon twist over the drink first to release its oils.
variations: Hugo: add fresh mint and lime and use Prosecco.

test-pilot.title: Test Pilot
test-pilot.description: A 1941 Don the Beachcomber tiki classic: dark and light rums with lime, Cointreau, falernum, a dash of bitters and a whisper of anise, flash-blended over ice.
steps: Put all the ingredients in a blender with the crushed ice.
Flash blend for 5 seconds, just to chill and froth it.
Pour into a double rocks glass, adding more crushed ice if needed, and garnish with a lime wheel.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Flash blend lime juice, falernum syrup, orange juice and a dash of bitters with crushed ice.

test-pilot.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Flash blending for just a few seconds chills and dilutes it without turning it into a slushie.
Measure the anise in drops, not dashes; a little goes a long way.
variations: Jet Pilot: add 1/2 oz grapefruit juice and 1/2 oz cinnamon syrup and skip the Cointreau.

three-dots-and-a-dash.title: Three Dots and a Dash
three-dots-and-a-dash.description: Don the Beachcomber's WWII victory drink, named for the Morse code "V": rhum agricole and dark rum with lime, orange, honey, falernum and allspice, garnished with three cherries and a pineapple dash.

ingredients.item: honey syrup (equal parts honey and hot water)

steps: Put all the ingredients in a blender with the crushed ice.
Flash blend for 5 seconds.
Pour into a tulip or tiki glass. Garnish with three cherries and a pineapple spear on a pick: the three dots and the dash.

cocktail.garnish: three cherries and a pineapple spear
cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Flash blend lime, orange juice, honey syrup, a pinch of allspice and crushed ice.

three-dots-and-a-dash.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Allspice dram is potent; measure it carefully.
The garnish spells "V" in Morse code: dot, dot, dot, dash.
variations: No blender: shake hard with crushed ice and pour everything into the glass.

tipperary.title: Tipperary
tipperary.description: An Irish cousin of the Manhattan from the early 1900s: Irish whiskey and sweet vermouth with a measure of herbal green Chartreuse, stirred and served up.

ingredients.item: vegan sweet vermouth (such as Dolin Rouge)

steps: Stir the whiskey, vermouth, Chartreuse and bitters with ice for 20 to 30 seconds.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
Express an orange twist over the top and drop it in.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Stir cold black tea with non-alcoholic red vermouth and a drop of herbal syrup.

tipperary.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Green Chartreuse is intense; start with 1/2 oz and adjust to taste.
Stirring keeps it silky and clear.
variations: The 1916 original uses equal parts whiskey, vermouth and Chartreuse for a bolder herbal drink.

woo-woo.title: Woo Woo
woo-woo.description: A fun, fruity 1980s highball: vodka and peach schnapps with cranberry juice over ice. Sweet, pink and easy.
steps: Fill a highball glass with ice.
Add the vodka, peach schnapps, cranberry juice and lime and stir well.
Garnish with a lime wedge.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Mix cranberry juice with a splash of peach nectar and lime over ice.

woo-woo.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: A squeeze of lime keeps it from being too sweet.
variations: Woo Woo shots: shake with ice and strain into shot glasses.

zaza.title: Zaza
zaza.description: A classic French café cocktail from the early 1900s: equal parts dry gin and Dubonnet Rouge, stirred cold with a twist of orange.
steps: Stir the gin, Dubonnet and bitters with ice for 20 to 30 seconds.
Strain into a chilled coupe or cocktail glass.
Express a lemon twist over the top and drop it in.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Stir cold red grape juice with a splash of tonic and a dash of orange syrup.

zaza.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Keep opened Dubonnet in the fridge; like vermouth, it fades after a few weeks.
Also known as the Dubonnet Cocktail, a favorite of Queen Elizabeth II, who preferred it over ice.
variations: Serve it on the rocks with a lemon slice, the royal way.
